title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
浙江武舉鄉試錄序
萬曆
天子御宇之元年法令載新民物
更始兩浙之士以文奮者羣
聚而賔于有司業已登諸
天府乃孟冬之月復舉武士如文
制御史蕭公廩先期檄郡邑
===
蒐羅剔扶官胄尺籍之夫十
一郡良家子如期而集登進
厥庭乃以右布政使江一麟
左叅政史朝宜提調按察司
副使滕伯輪僉事戴延容監
試暨大小執事罔敢不肅而
侍御公親監臨之三試而得
punctuated:
浙江武舉鄉試錄序
萬曆天子御宇之元年，法令載新，民物更始。兩浙之士以文奮者，羣聚而賔于有司，業已登諸天府；乃孟冬之月，復舉武士如文制。御史蕭公廩先期檄郡邑，蒐羅剔扶，官胄、尺籍之夫，十一郡良家子，如期而集，登進厥庭。乃以右布政使江一麟、左叅政史朝宜提調，按察司副使滕伯輪、僉事戴延容監試，暨大小執事，罔敢不肅；而侍御公親監臨之，三試而得
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Zhejiang Military Provincial Examination

In the first year of the reign of the Wanli Son of Heaven, the laws and ordinances were renewed, and the people and all things made a fresh start. The scholars of eastern and western Zhejiang who strove in civil letters gathered in groups to be received as guests by the authorities, and their names have already been entered into the Imperial Archives. Then, in the first month of winter, candidates in military arts were in turn examined and selected according to the system for the civil service. Ahead of time, Censor Mr. Xiao Lin 蕭廩 issued dispatches to the prefectures and districts to search out and select candidates; scions of hereditary military officers, men on the military registers, and sons of good families from all eleven prefectures assembled at the appointed time and were brought forward into the examination courtyard. Thereupon, Administration Vice Commissioner of the Right Jiang Yilin 江一麟 and Administration Vice Commissioner of the Left Shi Chaoyi 史朝宜 were appointed as Proctors, while Surveillance Vice Commissioner Teng Bolun 滕伯輪 and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Dai Yanrong 戴延容 served as Censorial Monitors, together with the greater and lesser functionaries, none daring to be anything less than reverent; and His Honor the Censor personally served as Supervising Official over the proceedings, conducting three sessions and…

title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
雋五十人以
獻蓋制雖由舊而
命則新矣一麟作而曰於休哉我
皇上神化之速
祖宗流澤之遠而至於斯也自有
三才以來立天以陰陽立地
以剛柔立人以仁義仁謂之
===
文義謂之武二者配陰陽剛
柔以成治世謂春舉以文秋
舉以武順天時也文出於南
武出於北應地氣也勘亂以
武守成以文別人材也殊不
知
帝德廣運風聲鼓舞而神化均泯
punctuated: 雋五十人以獻。蓋制雖由舊，而命則新矣。一麟作而曰：「於休哉！我皇上神化之速、祖宗流澤之遠，而至於斯也。自有三才以來，立天以陰陽，立地以剛柔，立人以仁義。仁謂之文，義謂之武，二者配陰陽、剛柔以成治。世謂春舉以文，秋舉以武，順天時也；文出於南，武出於北，應地氣也；勘亂以武，守成以文，別人材也。殊不知帝德廣運，風聲鼓舞，而神化均泯…
translation_en:
…fifty outstanding men to be presented to the throne. Indeed, although the institutional system followed old precedents, the imperial mandate was new!

[Jiang] Yilin 江一麟 rose and said: "Oh, how magnificent! The swiftness of Our Sovereign's divine transformation and the far-reaching flow of our Imperial Ancestors' beneficence have brought us to this! Ever since the Three Powers came into being, Heaven has been established through yin and yang, Earth through firmness and yielding, and Man through benevolence and righteousness. Benevolence is called civil (wen), and righteousness is called martial (wu); the two match yin and yang, firmness and yielding, so as to achieve good governance. The world says that holding examinations for civil talent in the spring and for martial talent in the autumn accords with the seasons of Heaven; that civil talent emerges from the south and martial talent emerges from the north in response to the terrestrial qi; and that suppressing rebellion through martial prowess and preserving achievements through civil administration distinguishes kinds of human talent. Yet people fail to realize that as the Imperial virtue broadly operates, its influence inspires and rouses all, and its divine transformation equally dissolves…

title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
於無迹故文非武不張武非
文不靖二者更相爲用豈繫
之於時而然耶且景龍升而
雲附猛虎嘯而風生豪傑之
士踵武於率
德熙庸於秉氣者豈以地爲限
哉我
===
皇上嗣服之初
詔頒天下卽以邊事爲飭此與有
周令主張皇六師之誥何異
邇又
納臺臣之疏崇奬武士使得推
舉如文例
聖謨
punctuated: 於無迹。故文非武不張，武非文不靖，二者更相爲用，豈繫之於時而然耶？且景龍升而雲附，猛虎嘯而風生，豪傑之士踵武於率德、熙庸於秉氣者，豈以地爲限哉？我皇上嗣服之初，詔頒天下，卽以邊事爲飭，此與有周令主張皇六師之誥何異？邇又納臺臣之疏，崇奬武士，使得推舉如文例，聖謨
translation_en:
…without leaving a trace. Therefore, civil governance cannot be extended without military might, and military might cannot bring peace without civil governance. The two serve each other in turn—how could this be bound merely to the seasons? Moreover, when the auspicious dragon ascends, clouds gather around it; when the fierce tiger roars, winds arise. Outstanding heroes who follow in the footsteps of those guided by Imperial virtue and achieve bright merit through their endowed vigor—how could they be limited by geography?

At the very beginning of His Majesty's succession to the throne, when edicts were promulgated throughout the realm, frontier affairs were immediately made the subject of strict admonition. How is this any different from the pronouncement of the enlightened rulers of the Zhou dynasty to glorify and magnify the Six Armies? Recently, His Majesty also accepted a memorial from Censorate officials to honor and encourage military men, allowing them to be recommended and promoted according to the same precedents as civil officials. His sacred counsels…

title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
神斷淵乎遠矣
明詔一日下千里而海隅日出之
地已喁喁思奮刮垢磨光以
應
上之求乃漸爲江南首重之邦昔
江漢之間誦文王之化自公
卿以及兎罝野人皆化於其
===
德編詩者首列於風而繫之
南言王化自北而南也周蓋
起於岐雍其民重厚質實號
爲興起而篤於仁義其後秦
襄公興師入定王室而行者
篤同仇之誼居者節于役之
感其勇健之氣見於阜鄰小
punctuated: 神斷，淵乎遠矣！明詔一日下千里，而海隅日出之地，已喁喁思奮，刮垢磨光，以應上之求。乃浙爲江南首重之邦，昔江漢之間，誦文王之化，自公卿以及兎罝野人，皆化於其德。編詩者首列於《風》而繫之《南》，言王化自北而南也。周蓋起於岐、雍，其民重厚質實，號爲興起而篤於仁義。其後秦襄公興師，入定王室，而行者篤同仇之誼，居者節于役之感，其勇健之氣見於《車鄰》、《小
translation_en: …and divine decisiveness—how deep and far-reaching they are! Once the illustrious decree was issued, traveling a thousand li in a single day, even in the lands by the sea where the sun rises, people were already eagerly looking up and yearning to rouse themselves, scraping away their grime and polishing their luster so as to answer His Majesty’s call. Now Zhejiang [written 漸] is the foremost state south of the Yangtze. In antiquity, in the region between the Yangtze and Han rivers, people sang praises of the transforming influence of King Wen; from high ministers and nobles down to the rustic men with rabbit-nets, all were transformed by his virtue. The compiler of the Odes placed these songs at the head of the "Airs of the States" (Feng) and attached them to the "South" (Nan), meaning that the royal transformation spread from north to south. Indeed, the Zhou arose in Qi and Yong, where the people were grave, generous, simple, and honest, known for rousing themselves to action and being steadfast in benevolence and righteousness. Later, when Duke Xiang of Qin raised an army and marched in to stabilize the royal house, those who went on the expedition held fast to the bond of sharing a common enemy, while those who stayed behind tempered their emotions regarding service on campaign; their brave and vigorous spirit was manifest in such odes as "Chariots Rumbling" (Che lin [written 阜鄰]) and "Small…

title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
戎諸詩循悍然可見當其盛
時奔走禦侮者豈無其人而
腹心干城之託獨兔罝之武
夫夫非南方之產歟且武夫
耳而以爲腹心其公侯蓋服
文王之教者至成王而綴衣
虎賁皆衛王宮而補王闕康
王述文武之烈而熊羆之士
卽爲不二心之臣夫以周世
尚文而其用武如此然則士
之興也其有由矣今浙固文
物之區也由周而上政教未
洽其稚魯慤愿之氣蓄而未
發入我
punctuated: 戎》諸詩，循悍然可見。當其盛時，奔走禦侮者豈無其人？而腹心干城之託，獨《兔罝》之武夫，夫非南方之產歟？且武夫耳，而以爲腹心，其公侯蓋服文王之教者。至成王，而綴衣、虎賁皆衛王宮而補王闕；康王述文、武之烈，而熊羆之士卽爲不二心之臣。夫以周世尚文，而其用武如此，然則士之興也，其有由矣。今浙固文物之區也，由周而上，政教未洽，其稚魯慤愿之氣蓄而未發。入我
translation_en: … "Small War Chariots" [Xiaorong], where their fierce spirit can still be clearly seen. During its flourishing era, how could there have been a lack of men who rushed about to fend off foreign aggression? Yet the trust of being "heart and mind" and "shield and wall" was placed solely in the martial men of the "Rabbit Snare" [Tuju] ode—and were they not natives of the south? Moreover, though they were merely martial men, they were regarded as trusted confidants; their dukes and marquises were surely those who had submitted to the teachings of King Wen. By the time of King Cheng, the keepers of the royal robes [zhuiyi] and the Gentlemen as Rapid as Tigers [huben] all guarded the royal palace and remedied the king's failings; when King Kang recounted the illustrious achievements of Kings Wen and Wu, the warriors like bears and grisly bears were none other than ministers of undivided loyalty. Now, given that the Zhou dynasty esteemed civil culture, yet employed military prowess in this manner, the rise of capable men certainly had its cause. Today, Zhejiang is indeed a region of refined culture and institutions. From the Zhou dynasty back into antiquity, governance and moral instruction had not yet fully penetrated it, so its simple, honest, and sincere spirit remained stored up and unexpressed. Upon entering our…

title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
明而脫穎舒翹者布滿寰宇然
猶類多觚槧之士出爲世用
顧武略若未遑者天下無事
或安於衣食湛於宴樂無所
用之乃今駸駸然用矣始多
士之至於斯也比其藝三試
之綺駢繡錯肅躬而入洋如
===
濟如視其騎震撼馳突有闗
陜之氣焉視其步穿揚破的
有三晉之材焉徐而閱其論
議縱規操矩參之以經書有
孫吳之遺而又進乎技矣蓋
天子居安思危
聖武布昭疎逖幽鬱覩
punctuated: 明，而脫穎舒翹者布滿寰宇。然猶類多觚槧之士，出爲世用，顧武略若未遑者。天下無事，或安於衣食，湛於宴樂，無所用之；乃今駸駸然用矣。始多士之至於斯也，比其藝，三試之，綺駢繡錯，肅躬而入，洋如濟如。視其騎，震撼馳突，有闗陜之氣焉；視其步，穿揚破的，有三晉之材焉；徐而閱其論議，縱規操矩，參之以經書，有孫、吳之遺，而又進乎技矣。蓋天子居安思危，聖武布昭，疎逖幽鬱，覩
translation_en: … Ming, those who stand out and display exceptional talent have filled the entire realm. Yet for the most part they have been men of writing tablets and scrolls who came forth to be of service to the world, while military strategy seemed something for which there was not yet leisure. When the realm was without incident, people perhaps rested content in clothing and food and steeped themselves in feasting and pleasure, having no occasion to make use of martial skills; now, however, they are increasingly being put to use. When the many gentlemen first arrived at this place, we compared their skills and tested them across three sessions. Arrayed like patterned silk and interlocking embroidery, they bowed respectfully and entered, grand and dignified in their bearing. Observing their mounted archery, shaking the ground as they galloped and charged, they possessed the spirit of Guanzhong and Shaanxi; observing their archery on foot, piercing the willow leaf and shattering the target, they possessed the talent of the Three Jin. Then, calmly reviewing their discourses and deliberations—unfolding the compass and wielding the square, integrating them with the Classics and histories—they possessed the legacy of Sunzi (孫子) and Wu Qi (吳起), and moreover had advanced beyond mere technical skill! This is because the Son of Heaven, dwelling in peace, remains mindful of danger; His Sacred Martiality is proclaimed and made manifest, so that even those in distant and obscure places, beholding…

title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
德嚮風其興也勃焉無問南北
愚於是徵
聖化之隆遠紹成周而疆理所加
殆或過之其物產之饒纖縞
織文布帛菽粟用以服食衣
被爲天下最至乃篠簜竹箭
之美羽革之奇又可以壯陣
===
容而共武服凡皆需供於
王府者也多士進豈無類是歟
乃者諸文士之進也侍御公
猶瞿然曰得無訾窳是用而
貢者有不任之罰矧士以蹐
跆舉者其宜懼尤甚也夫平
居則談韜鈐矜機略踔厲風
punctuated: 德嚮風，其興也勃焉，無問南北。愚於是徵聖化之隆，遠紹成周，而疆理所加，殆或過之。其物產之饒，纖縞織文、布帛菽粟，用以服食衣被，爲天下最；至乃篠簜竹箭之美、羽革之奇，又可以壯陣容而共武服，凡皆需供於王府者也。多士進，豈無類是歟？乃者，諸文士之進也，侍御公猶瞿然曰：「得無訾窳是用，而貢者有不任之罰？」矧士以蹐跆舉者，其宜懼尤甚也。夫平居則談韜鈐、矜機略，踔厲風
translation_en:
… his virtue and incline toward his transforming influence; their rise is vigorous and sudden, regardless of north or south. From this I see attested that the flourishing of His Majesty's transforming influence reaches far back to continue that of the成周 Cheng Zhou era, while the extent of the territories brought under governance perhaps even surpasses it. In the abundance of its products—fine white silks and patterned weaves, cloth, silk, beans, and grain used for food, clothing, and cover—this region is the foremost in the Empire. And as for the excellence of its small and large bamboos for arrows, and the rarity of its feathers and hides, these too can strengthen battle formations and supply military equipment; all are things required as tribute for the royal storehouses. As the many gentlemen advance here, how could they not be similar to these?

Recently, when the civil candidates were presented, His Honor the Regional Inspector (Censor) was still startled with concern, saying: "Could it be that flawed and inferior men are being employed, so that those who present them will incur the penalty for recommending the unfit?" How much more, then, for gentlemen recommended for their martial prowess in leaping and kicking—the reason for apprehension should be even greater! Now, in ordinary times they discuss the Six Secret Teachings (Taolüe) and boast of their strategic schemes, spirited and wind-…

title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
發若落落不可下設枹鼓有
警而伏綏振策無可以當國
士之用乃四顧招募若惟恐
後則世或絀南而略武無足
怪矣此愚所爲懼也雖然豪
傑之士不可以常度即古有
蹶張之夫亢多名碩所伏剱
===
天子
神武天縱御史暨諸從事奉宣惟
謹而浙又人物之區豈無魁
梧奇傑之士出而可以當干
城腹心之託如兎罝野人者
乎然則愚之懼可釋也是舉
也督撫副都御史方公〔弘靜〕
punctuated: 發，若落落不可下；設枹鼓有警，而伏綏振策，無可以當國士之用，乃四顧招募，若惟恐後，則世或絀南而略武，無足怪矣。此愚所爲懼也。雖然，豪傑之士，不可以常度。即古有蹶張之夫，亢多名碩所伏剱，天子神武天縱，御史暨諸從事奉宣惟謹，而浙又人物之區，豈無魁梧奇傑之士出，而可以當干城腹心之託，如兎罝野人者乎？然則愚之懼可釋也。是舉也，督撫副都御史方公〔弘靜〕
translation_en: … spirited and vigorous, appearing so aloof that they cannot be humbled; yet should there be an alarm of drumsticks and war drums, when it comes to grasping the carriage-mounting strap and cracking the whip, none of them can serve the function of a warrior of the state, so that one must look all around to recruit soldiers as if fearing only to be too late—then if the world sometimes disparages the South and neglects the military arts, it is hardly any wonder! This is what I fear. Even so, heroic and outstanding men cannot be measured by ordinary standards. Even in antiquity there were foot-cocked crossbowmen, and in the north [? 亢] there were many eminent worthies who leaned upon their swords [?]; now the Son of Heaven is divinely martial and heaven-endowed, the Censor and all the attendant officials reverently proclaim His majesty with utmost care, and Zhejiang is moreover a region of talent—how could there fail to emerge stalwart and extraordinary men who can shoulder the trust of being "shield and wall" and "heart and腹 (confidants)," like the rustic huntsmen of the "Rabbit Nets" (Tuju) ode? If so, then my fears may be dispelled. In this undertaking, the Supreme Commander and Grand Coordinator, Vice Censor-in-Chief His Excellency Fang (Fang Hongjing 方弘靜), …

title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
肅靖海氛風聲遠播督鹾御
史馬公應夢霜威日嚴武服
載飭清戎御史田公樂風猷
先達介士丕奮而工部員外
郎錢楷南京户部主事劉伯
縉皆榷稅玆土樂觀厥成左
布政使謝鵬舉右叅政蒙詔
===
左叅議劉宗岱按察使劉繼
文副使沈人种華汝礪劉翺
僉事沈奎王嘉言都指揮僉
事謝詔潘清張藻咸襄事於
外而右叅議徐雲程僉事徐
廷祼都指揮僉事魏堯相以
入
punctuated: 肅靖海氛，風聲遠播；督鹾御史馬公應夢，霜威日嚴，武服載飭；清戎御史田公樂，風猷先達，介士丕奮；而工部員外郎錢楷、南京户部主事劉伯縉，皆榷稅玆土，樂觀厥成；左布政使謝鵬舉、右叅政蒙詔、左叅議劉宗岱、按察使劉繼文、副使沈人种、華汝礪、劉翺、僉事沈奎、王嘉言、都指揮僉事謝詔、潘清、張藻，咸襄事於外；而右叅議徐雲程、僉事徐廷祼、都指揮僉事魏堯相以入
translation_en: … pacified the maritime disturbances, his renown spreading far and wide; Salt-Control Censor Mr. Ma Yingmeng 馬應夢, whose frost-like authority grows more severe by the day, has set military affairs in order; Military-Clearence Censor Mr. Tian Le 田樂, whose principled plans were set forth early on, has greatly roused the armored soldiers; while Vice Director in the Ministry of Works Qian Kai 錢楷 and Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue Liu Bojin 劉伯縉, both collecting commercial taxes in this territory, have delighted in witnessing its completion. Left Administration Commissioner Xie Pengju 謝鵬舉, Right Administration Vice Commissioner Meng Zhao 蒙詔, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Liu Zongdai 劉宗岱, Surveillance Commissioner Liu Jiwen 劉繼文, Surveillance Vice Commissioners Shen Renzhong 沈人种, Hua Ruli 華汝礪, and Liu Ao 劉翺, Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Shen Kui 沈奎 and Wang Jiayan 王嘉言, and Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Xie Zhao 謝詔, Pan Qing 潘清, and Zhang Zao 張藻 all assisted in the affair from the outside; while Right Assistant Administration Commissioner Xu Yuncheng 徐雲程, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Xu Tingguan 徐廷祼, and Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Wei Yaoxiang 魏堯相, on account of entering [the capital to offer] …

title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
賀副使趙宋以遷秩皆與聞盛
典者謹按故事書之列實宣
盛則督學在
浙江等處承宣布政使司右
布政使江一麟謹序
punctuated:

武舉事例

勘合條格

計開：

一、每遇子、午、卯、酉年十月武舉鄉試，預於九月内，各衛所起送都司，府州縣起送布政司，類送巡按御史，會同三司官考驗定數。仍行都司起送五府轉送兵部，布政司起送兵部。兩京衛所俱送中府，候到齊之日，中府掌印官會同各府并錦衣衛各掌印官，考驗定數，類送兵部。直隸衛所、留守司、大寧、萬全都司并各府州縣，俱各送巡按御史考驗定數，仍行各都司、直隸府州衛所照例起送。其十月内考驗日期并選取之法，一倣武舉會試例行。各處起送應武舉之人，務要詢訪素無過犯、操行端謹、言貌出衆、膂力過人，及考驗弓馬熟閑、答策通曉…
translation_en:
Precedents and Regulations for the Military Examinations

Verified Articles of Regulation

Itemized as follows:

1. Whenever the Military Provincial Examination is held in the tenth month of a zi, wu, mao, or you year, beforehand in the ninth month the various Guards and Battalions shall forward candidates to the Regional Military Commission, and the Prefectures, Subprefectures, and Districts shall forward candidates to the Provincial Administration Commission, which shall collectively forward them to the Regional Investigating Censor, who will join the officials of the Three Provincial Offices to examine and test them and determine their number. Thereafter, the Regional Military Commission shall be instructed to forward its candidates to the Five Chief Military Commissions for transfer to the Ministry of War, and the Provincial Administration Commission shall forward its candidates to the Ministry of War. The Guards and Battalions of the Two Capitals shall all send their candidates to the Central Chief Military Commission; when all have arrived, the Seal-holding Official of the Central Chief Military Commission shall join the Seal-holding Officials of each of the other Chief Military Commissions and the Embroidered-uniform Guard to examine and test them, determine their number, and collectively forward them to the Ministry of War. The Guards and Battalions of the Metropolitan Areas, the Regency, the Daning and Wanquan Regional Military Commissions, and the various Prefectures, Subprefectures, and Districts shall each send their candidates to the Regional Investigating Censor to examine and test them and determine their number, and the various Regional Military Commissions and the Metropolitan Prefectures, Subprefectures, Guards, and Battalions shall still be instructed to forward them in accordance with precedent. As for the dates of testing in the tenth month and the method of selection, everything shall be carried out in imitation of the precedents for the Military Metropolitan Examination. In forwarding candidates for the military examinations from the various localities, inquiries must be made to ensure that they have hitherto committed no offenses, are upright and circumspect in conduct, are outstanding in speech and appearance, and surpass others in physical strength, and upon testing are skilled in archery and horsemanship and well-versed in answering policy questions on…

Each of these qualifications must be clearly listed and annotated before they are permitted to be Courteously Forwarded; it is not permitted to indiscriminately recommend candidates without distinction merely to fill the quota. In the sixth month of the fourteenth year of the Zhengde reign (1519), the Ministry of War submitted a memorial stating that since the Military Provincial Examination was scheduled by regulation for the tenth month of that year, the procedural matters to be modeled after the Military Metropolitan Examination were itemized as follows:

1. It was deliberated and decided that for the Military Provincial Examination in the capital, following the precedent for examinations at the Military School, one Vice Minister of this Ministry, jointly with the Seal-holding Officials of the Five Chief Military Commissions and the Seal-holding Official of the Embroidered-uniform Guard, shall conduct the examination at the Eastern Official Hall of the Integrated Division; in Nanjing, the Nanjing Minister of War, jointly with the Seal-holding Officials of the Nanjing Chief Military Commissions and the Seal-holding Official of the Nanjing Embroidered-uniform Guard, shall conduct the examination at the Grand Drill Ground. The Censorate and the Nanjing Censorate shall each dispatch one Investigating Censor to monitor the examination. In the provinces, the Provincial Administration Commissions shall conduct the examinations at the local drill ground or Examination Compound; in the Directly Attached areas and along the various frontiers, the respective Regional Inspectors shall designate a centrally located and suitable place to conduct the examination. For the Military Provincial Examinations in the Two Capitals and various regions, the tea and meals for the examining officials, attending officers and soldiers, and candidates completing the final session of policy essays, as well as the required paper, brushes, inkstones, vermilion ink, and other items, shall in Beijing be provided by the various training divisions in accordance with established precedent, while in Nanjing they shall be at the disposal of the Nanjing Ministry of War…

As for the artisans and laborers who carve and print the examination questions, in both capitals they shall all be requisitioned from the prefectures and counties; in the provinces, the respective Regional Investigating Censors shall designate and requisition them, and the administrative officials for stamping the examination papers, sealing the candidates' names, and other such duties shall all follow established precedent.

The first session tests mounted archery, taking thirty-five paces as the standard; the second session tests foot archery, taking eighty paces as the standard. In each case, candidates must draw the bow to the full and level the arrow, and only shots that strike squarely in the center of the target shall count as hits; if there are arrows that graze the ground [? 創箭], or that hit the base of the target or the target flag, none of them shall be accepted. The third session tests one policy question. In the two capitals, following the precedent of the Integrated Division military examinations in previous years, officials of the Ministry of War shall set the question; in the provinces, the Regional Investigating Censors shall in all cases set the question. The policy question may either be based on ancient military treatises or inquire into current affairs; the essential point is that it be concise and suggestive, so as to observe the candidates' talent and insight, and there is no need to rely exclusively on hackneyed phrases on paper, merely selecting for rote memorization and thereby overlooking true talent. title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄

司府州縣衛所保送人員亦同本月
===
武宗皇帝聖旨這武舉鄉試條格都依擬行便
行與南京及在外各該衛門知道欽此今照
二十三日題奉
兵部侍郎爲本兵之佐既知武舉會
考難以又與武舉鄉試及查各處應
舉人員俱送巡按御史幷三司等官
考驗合將兩京衛所應試者亦送各
該巡按御史考試類送兵部其考驗

有先年已曾起送赴部會考不中之人，今次又來會試，許一體考驗起送。其考取之法，凡有五等，通照武舉會試。兩京各衛所保送各府，類送中府；上十衛幷武學，徑保送中府。其各衛所保送應舉人員，務要各開平素謀勇、習學騎射兵法，並無曾經問發等項緣由明白，及各處考語起送。在外司、府、州、縣、衛、所保送人員亦同。本月二十三日題，奉武宗皇帝聖旨：「這武舉鄉試條格都依擬行，便行與南京及在外各該衙門知道。欽此。」
今照兵部侍郎爲本兵之佐，既知武舉會考，難以又與武舉鄉試。及查各處應舉人員，俱送巡按御史幷三司等官考驗，合將兩京衛所應試者，亦送各該巡按御史考試，類送兵部。其考驗去處，幷執事等官、軍、匠役，及茶飯、紙
translation_en:
… Should there be individuals who in previous years were already forwarded to the Ministry for the joint examination (huikao) and failed to pass, and who now come again for the Metropolitan Examination, they are permitted to be tested and forwarded on an equal footing. As for the method of examination and selection, there are five grades in all, following throughout the rules of the Military Metropolitan Examination. The various guards and battalions (weisuo) in the two capitals shall recommend and forward candidates to their respective Chief Military Commissions (fu), which shall collectively forward them to the Central Chief Military Commission (Zhongfu); the Ten Imperial Guards (Shang shi wei) and the Military Schools (Wuxue) shall recommend and forward them directly to the Central Chief Military Commission. For the candidates recommended and forwarded by the various guards and battalions, each must clearly set forth his habitual strategic resourcefulness and bravery, his study and practice of mounted archery and the art of war, and the fact that he has never been convicted and sentenced to penal servitude or similar offenses, and be forwarded together with the evaluation remarks (kaoyu) from the respective offices. The same applies to personnel recommended and forwarded by the provincial agencies, prefectures, subprefectures, counties, guards, and battalions in the provinces. Memorialized on the twenty-third day of this month, we received the Sacred Edict of Emperor Wuzong: "These regulations for the Military Provincial Examination shall all be carried out as proposed. Promptly circulate them to Nanjing and the various offices concerned in the provinces for their information. Respect this!"

Now, considering that the Vice Minister of War (Bingbu shilang) is the assistant to the head of the Ministry of War, since he already administers (zhi) the Military Metropolitan Examination, it is difficult for him also to participate in the Military Provincial Examination. Furthermore, upon checking, candidates for the examination in the various provinces are all sent to the Regional Inspector (Xun'an yushi) together with officials of the Three Provincial Offices (Sansi) and others to be tested; therefore, candidates from the guards and battalions in the two capitals should likewise be sent to the respective Regional Inspectors to be examined and then collectively forwarded to the Ministry of War. As for the examination venues, together with the officiating officials, soldiers, artisans, and laborers, as well as tea and meals, paper…

translation_en:

者發回原籍當差取中之人行令該

會試之年照例於武舉場事畢日將
送到武生公同監試御史通行考驗
其不中者發回肄業中者不必分等

===

操三年之間獲有功次挨陞職級如
無功級但係訓練有成教師即補把
總把總即補千總月加米一石與武
舉一體保薦推用如或在營教練無
成不肯向上者聽督撫官徑自革回
起送之時各府州縣如敢狥情濫送

All the rest shall be distributed among the Capital Training Divisions and the various frontier commands under the designation of drill instructor, immediately serving as platoon commanders to train the soldiers. All shall be permitted to draw military rations and go on active duty and drill with the troops. If within three years they achieve military merit, they shall be promoted in rank in due order. title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
聽巡按御史指實糾治等因奉
穆宗皇帝聖旨是這武生係每會同監試御史
驗果有勇力技能的咨送薊鎮軍門再行覈
實徑自去留京營及各邊且不必發去欽此
punctuated: 聽巡按御史指實糾治等因。奉穆宗皇帝聖旨：「是。這武生，係每會同監試御史驗果有勇力技能的，咨送薊鎮軍門再行覈實，徑自去留；京營及各邊且不必發去。欽此。」
translation_en: … allow the Regional Inspector to point out the facts and impeach and punish them, and so forth. In response, an Imperial Edict of Emperor Muzong was received: "Approved. As for these military students, you [係每, sc. 爾每?] together with the Examination-supervising Censors shall test them; those who truly possess courage, strength, and martial skills shall be sent by official communication to the Supreme Commander's headquarters at the Jizhou Defense Command for further verification, where they may directly decide whom to retain or dismiss. For now, there is no need to dispatch them to the Capital Training Divisions or the various frontier commands. Respect this."

title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試題名
第壹場
試馬上箭以三十五步爲則中四箭以上
者合式
第貳場
試步下箭以八十步爲則中二箭以上者
合式
第叁場
策二道
===
問兵者守國之備古之聖王內寧外謐
而享國無虞者以教訓有素而常勝
之道在我也故大司馬法四時簡閱
各有所取非直爲張皇之具而已春
秋去古未遠簡兵宗丘教民三事者
猶有先王遺意今其詳有可言者與
後此有從六郡良家子材官之士馳
射上林者有閱武城西者有親閱諸
軍參攷勞績升絀之者不知視古制
punctuated:
萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試題名

第壹場：試馬上箭，以三十五步爲則，中四箭以上者合式。
第貳場：試步下箭，以八十步爲則，中二箭以上者合式。
第叁場：策二道。

問：兵者，守國之備。古之聖王內寧外謐而享國無虞者，以教訓有素，而常勝之道在我也。故《大司馬法》四時簡閱，各有所取，非直爲張皇之具而已。春秋去古未遠，簡兵宗丘、教民三事者，猶有先王遺意，今其詳有可言者與？後此，有從六郡良家子、材官之士馳射上林者，有閱武城西者，有親閱諸軍、參攷勞績升絀之者，不知視古制…
translation_en:
Topics of the Zhejiang Military Provincial Examination of the First Year of the Wanli Era (1573)

First Session: Testing mounted archery, with thirty-five paces as the standard; those hitting the target with four or more arrows qualify.
Second Session: Testing dismounted archery, with eighty paces as the standard; those hitting the target with two or more arrows qualify.
Third Session: Two policy questions.

Question: Soldiers are the preparedness by which a state is defended. That the sage kings of antiquity achieved internal tranquility and external peace, enjoying their realms without anxiety, was because their training was well-established and the way of constant victory lay within themselves. Therefore, in the methods of the Grand Minister of War (Da Sima), the seasonal inspections and reviews of troops each had their specific purpose, and were not merely tools for ostentatious display. The Spring and Autumn period was not yet far removed from antiquity; inspecting troops at Zongqiu [?] and instructing the people in the three matters still retained the lingering intent of the former kings. Can the details of these be recounted today? Later than this, there were those who galloped and shot arrows in the Shanglin Park accompanied by youths from respectable families of the six commanderies and skilled soldiers (caiguan); there were those who reviewed the military west of the city; and there were those who personally reviewed the various armies, examining and verifying their merits and achievements to promote or demote them. One wonders how these compare to the ancient institutions…

title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
何如且當時六軍之所練習者又果
有濟於用否與我
國家講武之儀歲時不廢載在令甲者至爲
詳悉宜其赫赫洸洸而靖國禦侮之
足恃也但一遇警急非苦脆弱則苦
空虛召募調集之舉若出於必不可
已則平日之所教所養豈盡無當于
實與夫教民七年可以即戎夫子之言
之令召募調集於一旦而使鉞臨戎
者咸賴此以爲臨敵制勝之長策是
兵可不教而戰令甲可弛也諸士抱
藝而來行將有斧鉞之寄則簡閱之
教不可或後其詳譚之以觀爾韜鈐
之略
===
問孔子於軍旅曰未學而行三軍則與
夫好謀而成然則兵之尚謀有自來
矣觀春秋所載戰伐之事莫盛於齊
桓晉文召陵之師書晉進書次書遂傳
punctuated:
何如？且當時六軍之所練習者，又果有濟於用否與？我國家講武之儀，歲時不廢，載在令甲者，至爲詳悉，宜其赫赫洸洸，而靖國禦侮之足恃也。但一遇警急，非苦脆弱，則苦空虛，召募調集之舉，若出於必不可已，則平日之所教所養，豈盡無當于實與？夫「教民七年，可以即戎」，夫子之言之，令召募調集於一旦，而使鉞臨戎者，咸賴此以爲臨敵制勝之長策，是兵可不教而戰，令甲可弛也。諸士抱藝而來，行將有斧鉞之寄，則簡閱之教不可或後。其詳譚之，以觀爾韜鈐之略。

問：孔子於軍旅曰「未學」，而行三軍則與夫「好謀而成」，然則兵之尚謀，有自來矣。觀《春秋》所載戰伐之事，莫盛於齊桓、晉文。召陵之師，書晉進、書次、書遂，傳
translation_en:
…how do they compare? Moreover, was what the Six Armies practiced at that time truly of any practical avail? Our dynasty's ceremonies for military training are never neglected in their seasonal observance, and what is recorded in the statutes is detailed in the extreme. One would expect them to be awe-inspiring and martial, reliable enough for pacifying the state and repelling foreign aggression. Yet the moment an urgent alarm arises, we suffer either from weakness or from depleted ranks, and the measures of recruiting mercenaries and calling up transferred troops seem to become unavoidable. Could it be that what is taught and nurtured in peacetime is entirely devoid of practical substance? Now, "After a good man has taught the common people for seven years, they may be led to war"—so the Master spoke of it. If instead we recruit and assemble troops in a single morning, and those who wield the battle-axe to take command in the field all rely on this as their grand strategy for facing the enemy and securing victory, this would mean that soldiers can fight without being trained and that the statutes can be relaxed! You gentlemen have come here bearing your martial skills and will soon be entrusted with the command of the battle-axe; thus, instruction in military review and inspection must not be neglected. Discuss this in detail, so that we may observe your grasp of military strategy.

Question: Regarding military affairs, Confucius said he had "not studied" them, yet when leading the Three Armies he approved of those who "delight in planning and bring things to completion." Thus, the high value placed on strategy in warfare has a long history. Looking at the military campaigns recorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu), none were more prominent than those of Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin. In the campaign of Shaoling, the chronicle records "advanced" [reading 晉進 as 進?], records "halted," and records "thereupon"; the commentary…

title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
者謂其奇正竝用是果然歟至城濮
之戰則純用詭道以取勝矣自夫子
有正譎之論而二伯之優劣遂定然
齊桓之伯也謀之三十年而後成而
楚人滅黃其身已不能救晉文五年
而用其民一戰勝楚遂主夏盟其後
襄文公之餘威得爲諸侯盟主者又
二十餘年其故何歟後世兵家者流
大率祖用二法亦莫盛於淮陰孔明
===
孔明之兵祖管仲而韓信之謀似先
軫隆中自比之略與泜上論兵之法
可得而言之歟然信一出而破趙下
齊并魏取楚孔明卒不能越尺寸以
取中原說者謂其所遇不同其果然
歟抑管葛用正而軫信用奇其取威
制勝之效終不同歟歐陽公作五代
史敘王彥章德勝之戰有感於西事
嘗恨諸將不能出奇而李衛公對唐
punctuated: 者謂其奇正竝用，是果然歟？至城濮之戰，則純用詭道以取勝矣。自夫子有正譎之論，而二伯之優劣遂定。然齊桓之伯也，謀之三十年而後成，而楚人滅黃，其身已不能救；晉文五年而用其民，一戰勝楚，遂主夏盟，其後襄文公之餘威，得爲諸侯盟主者又二十餘年，其故何歟？後世兵家者流，大率祖用二法，亦莫盛於淮陰、孔明。孔明之兵祖管仲，而韓信之謀似先軫。隆中自比之略，與泜上論兵之法，可得而言之歟？然信一出而破趙、下齊、并魏、取楚，孔明卒不能越尺寸以取中原，說者謂其所遇不同，其果然歟？抑管、葛用正，而軫、信用奇，其取威制勝之效終不同歟？歐陽公作《五代史》，敘王彥章德勝之戰，有感於西事，嘗恨諸將不能出奇；而李衛公對唐
translation_en: … commentators say that he employed both the unorthodox and the orthodox together—is this truly so? When it came to the Battle of Chengpu, however, victory was won purely through the way of deception. Ever since the Master [Confucius] pronounced his judgment on uprightness versus craftiness, the relative merits of the two hegemons have been settled. Yet for Duke Huan of Qi (Qi Huan) to achieve hegemony, he planned for thirty years before succeeding, and when the men of Chu destroyed Huang, he himself was already unable to save it; whereas Duke Wen of Jin (Jin Wen) employed his people after five years, defeated Chu in a single battle, and thereupon presided over the covenant of the Chinese states, and afterward, relying on the lingering awe of Duke Wen, Duke Xiang was able to remain leader of the feudal lords' covenant for more than twenty years longer—what is the reason for this? In later ages, military strategists have generally modeled themselves on and employed these two methods, and none flourished more than Marquis of Huaiyin [Han Xin 韓信] and Kongming [Zhuge Liang 諸葛亮]. Kongming's warfare took Guan Zhong 管仲 as its ancestor, while Han Xin's strategy resembled that of Xian Zhen 先軫. Can you recount the grand strategy in which he compared himself [to Guan Zhong and Yue Yi] at Longzhong, and the principles of warfare discussed on the Zhi River? Yet once Han Xin went forth, he shattered Zhao, subjugated Qi, annexed Wei, and took Chu, whereas Kongming in the end could not advance even a foot or an inch to take the Central Plains. Commentators say that the circumstances they encountered were different—is this truly so? Or is it that Guan Zhong and Zhuge Liang employed the orthodox, while Xian Zhen and Han Xin employed the unorthodox, so that their effectiveness in commanding awe and securing victory was ultimately different? When Ouyang Xiu (Ouyang gong 歐陽公) composed the History of the Five Dynasties (Wudai shi 五代史) and narrated Wang Yanzhang's 王彥章 battle at Desheng, moved by the events in the west [against Western Xia], he once regretted that the generals were unable to devise unorthodox maneuvers; whereas when Duke Wei of Li (Li Weigong 李衛公, i.e., Li Jing 李靖) replied to Tang …

title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
太宗則謂諸將多不知以奇爲正以
正爲奇奇正又果一道歟諸士子居
則談兵行將舉而用諸試爲我言之
以資抵掌
論
五者知勝之道
punctuated:
太宗，則謂諸將多不知以奇爲正、以正爲奇，奇正又果一道歟？諸士子居則談兵，行將舉而用諸，試爲我言之，以資抵掌。

論

五者知勝之道。
translation_en:
… Taizong 唐太宗, said that most generals did not know how to make the unorthodox into the orthodox and the orthodox into the unorthodox. Are the unorthodox and the orthodox, then, truly a single principle? In daily life you gentlemen discuss military affairs, and soon you will be selected to put them into practice; try to explain these matters for me, so as to provide material for animated discussion.

Discourse

"These five are the way to know victory."

title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
第叅場
策
第一問
周　書
馬上中四箭
步下中二箭
今天下之名存而實亡者孰有甚於簡閱
之令也天下無事誠無事兵若不必核實
以求精者但今北虜雖已款塞而猾夏之
===
防不可或弛東南山海之寇雖漸就平而
姦宄之慮不可不豫若不先事於無事之
日而泄泄然惟虛文之飾則卒有警急能
無倉皇潰亂之虞耶執事策士而首及于
此誠未雨桑土之思也敢不畢陳所聞傳
曰天生五材民並用之誰能去兵故大司
馬之法載於周官而車攻吉日之詩咏宣
王脩攘之政最為詳悉則兵也者誠守國
衛民之所不可廢者也然兵固不可廢而
punctuated:
第叅場
策
第一問
周書，馬上中四箭，步下中二箭。
今天下之名存而實亡者，孰有甚於簡閱之令也？天下無事，誠無事兵，若不必核實以求精者。但今北虜雖已款塞，而猾夏之防不可或弛；東南山海之寇雖漸就平，而姦宄之慮不可不豫。若不先事於無事之日，而泄泄然惟虛文之飾，則卒有警急，能無倉皇潰亂之虞耶？執事策士而首及于此，誠未雨桑土之思也，敢不畢陳所聞？傳曰：「天生五材，民並用之，誰能去兵？」故大司馬之法載於《周官》，而《車攻》、《吉日》之詩咏宣王脩攘之政，最為詳悉。則兵也者，誠守國衛民之所不可廢者也。然兵固不可廢，而
translation_en:
Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Zhou Shu 周書 (hit the target with four arrows on horseback, and with two arrows on foot).
In the empire today, among those things whose name survives while their substance is lost, what could be worse than the ordinances for military inspection and review? When the empire is at peace and there is truly no need for military action, it might seem unnecessary to verify realities in order to seek elite troops. Yet today, although the northern caitiffs have submitted at the frontier passes, defenses against their disturbing the Chinese states must never be relaxed; and although the mountain and sea bandits of the southeast have gradually been pacified, precautions against traitorous villains must be prepared in advance. If we do not attend to matters beforehand during days of peace, and instead lazily indulge only in the embellishment of empty formalities, then should a sudden emergency arise, how could we avoid the danger of panicked collapse and disorder? In putting policy questions to the candidates, Your Excellency has addressed this first of all; this is truly the foresight of gathering mulberry root-bark before it rains. How dare I not set forth everything I have heard? The commentary says: "Heaven produces the five materials, and the people use them all; who can do away with weapons?" Thus the methods of the Minister of War (Da Sima 大司馬) are recorded in the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan 周官), and the odes "Our Chariots Were Strong" (Chegong 車攻) and "A Lucky Day" (Jiri 吉日) sing of King Xuan's 宣王 governance in cultivating internal rule and repelling external foes in the greatest detail. Military force, therefore, is truly something that cannot be dispensed with in defending the state and protecting the people. Yet while military force certainly cannot be dispensed with, …

title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
先王亦不以兵輕試于天下寓之於農練
之於農隙春曰振旅夏曰茇止秋曰治兵
冬曰大閱名雖不同無非敎者是以先王
之兵不用則靜而不可測用則動而不可
制何者練之有素而耳目心意之用如一
人也春秋去古未遠列國大夫爲國将兵
者猶知簡閱遺意然毋簡上國之兵于宗
丘息民五年而後用師楚兵遂稱競於天
下子犯於晉文始入而欲用其民也始而
===
示之以義繼而示之以信終而示之以禮
故今年出穀戍明年釋宋圍城濮之烈君
子曰文之敎也彼之不敎而戰者卒以糜
爛其民旨貽削弱之憂兵豈可以不習哉
自茲而降兵制更變不常簡閱之法大非
古者四時之敎漢之文帝唐之太宗宋之
太祖皆身承兵革之餘操心危而慮患深
故於閱武之事猶知所重從六郡良家子
材官之士馳射上林非以騁技也閱武城
punctuated: 先王亦不以兵輕試于天下。寓之於農，練之於農隙。春曰振旅，夏曰茇止，秋曰治兵，冬曰大閱，名雖不同，無非敎者。是以先王之兵，不用則靜而不可測，用則動而不可制。何者？練之有素，而耳目心意之用如一人也。春秋去古未遠，列國大夫爲國将兵者，猶知簡閱遺意。然毋簡上國之兵于宗丘，息民五年而後用師，楚兵遂稱競於天下。子犯於晉文始入而欲用其民也，始而示之以義，繼而示之以信，終而示之以禮。故今年出穀戍，明年釋宋圍，城濮之烈，君子曰：「文之敎也。」彼之不敎而戰者，卒以糜爛其民，旨貽削弱之憂，兵豈可以不習哉？自茲而降，兵制更變不常，簡閱之法大非古者四時之敎。漢之文帝、唐之太宗、宋之太祖，皆身承兵革之餘，操心危而慮患深，故於閱武之事猶知所重。從六郡良家子、材官之士馳射上林，非以騁技也；閱武城
translation_en:
… the Former Kings also did not lightly test their troops upon the realm. They lodged military service within agriculture and trained soldiers during the intervals between farming seasons. In spring it was called "marshaling the hosts" (zhenlü), in summer "bivouacking in the grass" (bazhi), in autumn "drilling the troops" (zhibing), and in winter "the grand review" (dayue). Though the names differed, none of them was anything other than instruction. Therefore, as for the troops of the Former Kings, when not employed they were still and unfathomable; when employed they moved and could not be checked. Why was this? Because their training was well established, and the use of their ears, eyes, minds, and intentions was as if that of a single man.

In the Spring and Autumn period, which was not yet far removed from antiquity, the grandees of the various states who commanded troops for their countries still understood the inherited principle of military inspection and review. Ran Wu [Dou Lian] inspected the troops of the upper state at Zongqiu, resting the people for five years before employing the army, and the troops of Chu were thereupon acclaimed as the strongest in the realm. As for Zifan [Hu Yan], when Duke Wen of Jin first re-entered his state and wished to employ his people, he first showed them righteousness, next showed them trustworthiness, and finally showed them ritual propriety. Thus in one year he drove out the garrison at Gu, and the next year he relieved the siege of Song; of the glorious achievement at Chengpu, the gentleman said: "It was the instruction of Duke Wen." As for those who go to war without instructing the people, they end up mangling their populace and bringing upon themselves [?] the sorrow of territorial reduction and weakness. How could troops possibly not be drilled?

From that time onward, military institutions changed unpredictably, and the methods of inspection and review were vastly different from the ancient instruction across the four seasons. Yet Emperor Wen of Han, Taizong of Tang, and Taizu of Song all personally inherited the aftermath of armed conflict; they kept their minds alert to peril and took deep precautions against calamity, and thus regarding the matter of military reviews they still knew to attach importance to it. Being accompanied by the sons of good families from the six commanderies and the skilled soldiers (caiguan) in riding and shooting in the Shanglin Park was not for showing off skill; reviewing troops to the west of the city…

練不休視先王教止四時者更爲頻數宜

州邑者果安在哉夫兵有主客有召募有
punctuated: 西，非以觀兵也；親閱諸軍，參攷勞績升絀之，非以明功次之典也。倡之使作其氣，練之使盡其材，故當其時，兵皆可用，而威行四遠，創守之勳聲稱於後世者，非其教閱之明故□章者與？我國家□□之令，內自畿輔，外自邊徼之地，有將領以統之，憲臣以督之，非隆寒大暑，操練不休，視先王教止四時者，更爲頻數。宜其勁卒克於行伍，而空虛脆弱非所患矣。何曩者東西三鎮告急，膺筦鑰之司者深懷震恐，遠徵近調，羽檄交馳于途，甚至懸重格以募勇敢，亦鮮有振纓挾策應者，則平日之所術循、所振勵，果皆不足恃矣乎？淛、直、閩、粤之事，嘯聚剽刼，隨樸而輙起，少熄而復熾者，已多年於玆。方槍攘紛紜之時，議調遣、議召募，是也；及今有事，而調遣召募猶不能已，則平日之隷籍戎行、編名州邑者，果安在哉？夫兵有主客，有召募，有
translation_en:
… west of the city was not merely to make a display of military might; personally inspecting the various armies, examining their merits and achievements to promote or demote them, was not merely to clarify the statutes of merit gradations. By taking the lead, they roused the soldiers' morale; by drilling them, they brought out their full capabilities. Thus, in their times, the troops were all fit for use, their prestige extended far and wide, and their accomplishments in founding and defending the realm were praised in later generations—was this not the manifestly illustrious result [?] of their clear instruction and inspection?

Under the ordinances of [?] in our dynasty, from the capital region within to the frontier marches without, there are commanders to lead the troops and censorial officials to supervise them. Except in the depth of winter and the height of summer, drilling never ceases, making it even more frequent than under the former kings, whose instruction was limited to the four seasons. It ought to be that strong soldiers fill the ranks [?], and that depletion and weakness are nothing to worry about. Why was it, then, that in the past when the three eastern and western frontier garrisons reported emergencies, those charged with the responsibility of guarding the strategic keys were gripped by deep terror, requisitioning troops from afar and transferring them from nearby, with feathered dispatches crisscrossing on the roads—and even when heavy rewards were posted to recruit the brave, few adjusted their cap tassels and came forward with strategies in response? Were the methods followed [?] and the encouragements given in ordinary times truly all unreliable?

In the affairs of Zhejiang, Nan Zhili, Fujian, and Guangdong, bandits have banded together to plunder and rob; no sooner are they beaten down [?] than they rise again, subsiding a little only to flare up anew, and this has gone on now for many years. title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
士著固皆可用以摧鋒創敵者也今主兵
其耗弛獨以調遣召募爲固圉禦侮之長
策不知此可倖於目前而以爲久遠之畫
則非矣盖應調之兵非我族類彼豈有親
戚丘隴之顧乎其心日夜干賞蹈利已也
至於應募而來者尤多無籍非亡命則惡
少耳縱横睥睨乃其故習垂首於法制之
安者能幾人也矧購募之必重犒賞之必
厚鎧仗之必給需求之必煩村塢之必擾
皆調遣召募之所必至者昔日之弊歴歴
可陳兹乃安焉玩志於蕭艾之圖託言於
采薇之役則
===
國家簡閲令甲不幾於虛設而夫子所謂教
民七年可以即戎者非耶愚嘗謂今日南
北雖稱寧謐而訓練不可緩也訓練之事
不可緩而主兵士著尤其要也但主兵士
著久棄不習一旦欲起而率作之績効非
punctuated: 士著，固皆可用以摧鋒創敵者也。今主兵其耗弛，獨以調遣、召募爲固圉禦侮之長策。不知此可倖於目前，而以爲久遠之畫，則非矣。盖應調之兵，非我族類，彼豈有親戚、丘隴之顧乎？其心日夜干賞蹈利已也。至於應募而來者，尤多無籍，非亡命則惡少耳。縱横睥睨，乃其故習，垂首於法制之安者，能幾人也？矧購募之必重，犒賞之必厚，鎧仗之必給，需求之必煩，村塢之必擾，皆調遣、召募之所必至者，昔日之弊，歴歴可陳。兹乃安焉，玩志於蕭艾之圖，託言於《采薇》之役，則國家簡閲令甲，不幾於虛設？而夫子所謂「教民七年，可以即戎」者，非耶？愚嘗謂：今日南北雖稱寧謐，而訓練不可緩也；訓練之事不可緩，而主兵、士著尤其要也。但主兵、士著久棄不習，一旦欲起而率作之，績効非
translation_en: …and local troops [士著, read 土著], all of which can indeed be used to break the enemy's vanguard and inflict casualties. Today, the regular garrison troops have become depleted and lax, and reliance is placed solely on transferring troops from elsewhere and recruiting mercenaries as the long-term strategy for securing the borders and repelling aggression. People fail to realize that while this may by luck suffice for the immediate present, to take it as a permanent plan is wrong. For troops that answer a transfer summons are not of our own kith and kin; how could they have any regard for our relatives or ancestral graves? Their minds are day and night bent only on seeking rewards and pursuing profit. As for those who come in response to recruitment, even more of them are unregistered vagrants—if not fugitives, then young ruffians. Acting unrestrainedly and looking down on everything with arrogance is their old habit; how many of them are willing to bow their heads and abide peacefully by the laws and regulations? Moreover, recruitment bounties must be heavy, rewards and provisions must be generous, armor and weapons must be supplied, requisitions and demands will inevitably be burdensome, and villages and hamlets will inevitably be harassed—all of these are the inevitable consequences of transferring and recruiting troops, and the abuses of past days can be enumerated one by one. If we now rest content with this, indulging our minds in makeshift plans as worthless as mugwort and making excuses about the hardships of border campaigns like those in the ode "Gathering Thorn-ferns" (Caiwei), then are the Dynasty's statutes on military inspection and review not almost reduced to an empty formality? And was the Master [Confucius] wrong when he said, "When a good man has taught the people for seven years, they may also be employed in war"? I have always maintained that although the north and south are today said to be peaceful and quiet, military training cannot be delayed; and while the business of training cannot be delayed, regular garrison troops and local militia are especially crucial. However, regular garrison troops and local militia have long been neglected and unpracticed; if one morning we wish to rouse them and lead them into action, the results cannot…

title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
可近觀列營之兵半皆虛籍而役占之難
稽逃亡之弗察孰非耗兵之端乎兵日耗
則部伍日缺即有一二存者惟擄妻抱子
老矣兵革之任非所閑也且著之名曰保
甲曰弓兵曰機兵是已三者法雖立而無
裨實用名雖存而祗供追呼及問其所以
敎之練之者群趨迭閧若將爲戲止耳嗟
夫其敝若此有閱武之責者將何如而後
可曰委任之權在上而核實之政在下而
===
已兵志曰法不可以從中制權不可以縱
外御言責成之當專也乃今之待憲臣將
領者輕矣事多狗於掣肘憲臣且束手莫
展也而況於將領乎是必擇其可用之才
而勿慽其得爲之具予之以便宜專之以
賞罰信之以始終則憲臣將領之權重而
後核實之政上固可以責之下亦可以行
之設有不効其罰也奚辭夫所謂核實者
稽影射革包占禁挑選復逋逃此固主兵
punctuated: 可近觀。列營之兵，半皆虛籍，而役占之難稽，逃亡之弗察，孰非耗兵之端乎？兵日耗則部伍日缺，即有一二存者，惟擄妻抱子，老矣，兵革之任，非所閑也。且著之名，曰保甲，曰弓兵，曰機兵是已。三者法雖立而無裨實用，名雖存而祗供追呼，及問其所以敎之練之者，群趨迭閧，若將爲戲止耳。嗟夫！其敝若此，有閱武之責者，將何如而後可？曰：委任之權在上，而核實之政在下而已。《兵志》曰：「法不可以從中制，權不可以縱外御。」言責成之當專也。乃今之待憲臣將領者輕矣，事多狗於掣肘，憲臣且束手莫展也，而況於將領乎？是必擇其可用之才，而勿慽其得爲之具，予之以便宜，專之以賞罰，信之以始終，則憲臣將領之權重，而後核實之政，上固可以責之，下亦可以行之。設有不効，其罰也奚辭？夫所謂核實者，稽影射、革包占、禁挑選、復逋逃，此固主兵
translation_en:
…can be seen in the short term. Half the soldiers in the arrayed camps exist only as empty names on the registers; with the difficulty of auditing those privately requisitioned for labor and the failure to investigate desertions, which of these is not a cause of troop depletion? As the troops are depleted day by day, the ranks grow more deficient by the day. Even if one or two remain, they merely cling to their wives and hold their children, grown old; the duties of arms and armor are something in which they have no training. As for the designations of the local militia [? 著, for 土著], they are none other than the mutual-security tithings (baojia), archers (gongbing), and tactical militia (jibing). Although the regulations for these three have been established, they are of no benefit to practical use; although their names survive, they merely serve for running errands at the summons of officials. And when one asks how they are instructed and trained, they rush about in crowds and raise a clamor in turns, as if merely playing a game, and nothing more.

Alas! With abuses such as these, how should those who bear the responsibility of inspecting the military proceed so that things may be set right? I say: the authority to delegate responsibility lies above, while the administration of verifying realities lies below—that is all. The Treatise on the Military (Bingzhi) states: "Operations cannot be controlled from the court inside, nor can authority be directed from outside [?]." This means that holding officials accountable for results must be backed by exclusive authority. Yet nowadays, surveillance officials and military commanders are treated lightly. In their affairs they are often hampered by interference and constraints [? 狗於掣肘]; even surveillance officials have their hands tied and cannot desplegar their abilities, how much more so the military commanders? Therefore, we must select talents who are capable of serving and not begrudge [? 慽, for 奪/惜] them the means by which they can act—granting them discretionary power, giving them sole authority over rewards and punishments, and trusting them from beginning to end. Then the authority of surveillance officials and commanders will carry weight, and only afterward can the administration of verifying realities be demanded of them from above and carried out by them below. If by chance they fail to produce results, what excuse could they offer to escape punishment?

Now, what is meant by verifying realities: auditing fraudulent exemptions and substitutions, abolishing private monopolization of soldiers, prohibiting the skimming of elite troops [?], and recovering deserters—these are indeed the…

title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
之大端也重招撫明部隊去應役時巡行
此固主著之大端也然又有不盡於此者
兵家之法超忽變化目駭耳廻茍非素知
臨敵必亂是必如李抱真之練澤潞兵李
德裕之練雄邊子弟晉齊王之練武定軍
宋慶曆之練保毅軍宣毅軍而後兵爲有
濟核實者非虛也不然核實之政亦晝餅
之類而已又何貴於核實哉二者練矣夫
是則調集可以漸遣召募可以或停轉餉
===
可省而騷擾亦可息也議者茍不先核實
於主兵主著之求而遽謂調集召募之可
去譬之病者宿艾未積而謝去遠醫萬一
疾作廼汲汲然裹糧求之抑又晚矣雖然
天下之事有機得其機而運之萬里之外
無不應者訓練之政執事固慮其無當於
實也茍
國家以兵戎重務當閑暇之時爲衣茹之計
請
punctuated: 之大端也；重招撫、明部隊、去應役、時巡行，此固主著之大端也。然又有不盡於此者。兵家之法，超忽變化，目駭耳廻，茍非素知，臨敵必亂。是必如李抱真之練澤潞兵、李德裕之練雄邊子弟、晉齊王之練武定軍、宋慶曆之練保毅軍、宣毅軍，而後兵爲有濟，核實者非虛也。不然，核實之政，亦晝餅之類而已，又何貴於核實哉？二者練矣，夫是則調集可以漸遣，召募可以或停，轉餉可省，而騷擾亦可息也。議者茍不先核實於主兵、主著之求，而遽謂調集、召募之可去，譬之病者宿艾未積，而謝去遠醫，萬一疾作，廼汲汲然裹糧求之，抑又晚矣。雖然，天下之事有機，得其機而運之，萬里之外無不應者。訓練之政，執事固慮其無當於實也。茍國家以兵戎重務，當閑暇之時爲衣茹之計，請
translation_en:
… the main points regarding the regular garrison troops (zhubing); and emphasizing pacification and recruitment, clarifying unit organization, eliminating menial labor assignments, and conducting timely patrols—these are indeed the main points regarding the local indigenous troops [?; zhuzhuo]. Yet there is still more to it than this. The methods of military strategists are sudden and ever-changing, dazzling the eyes and dizzying the ears; if the troops are not already familiar with them, they will surely fall into chaos when facing the enemy. Therefore, one must train them as Li Baozhen 李抱真 trained the troops of Zelu 澤潞, as Li Deyu 李德裕 trained the Valiant Border Youths (Xiongbian zidi), as the Prince of Qi of the Jin [?; Jin Qiwang 晉齊王] trained the Wuding Army (Wuding jun), and as in the Qingli 慶曆 reign of the Song they trained the Baoyi Army (Baoyi jun) and Xuanyi Army (Xuanyi jun). Only then will the troops be effective, and the verification of realities (heshi) will not be in vain. Otherwise, a policy of verifying realities will be no more than a painted餅 [畫餅, cake] and the like—what value would there be in verifying realities?

Once both forces are well trained, then the mobilized reinforcements (diaoji) can gradually be sent home, the hired recruits (zhaomu) can perhaps be discontinued, the transport of military provisions can be economized, and disturbances to the populace can also be brought to rest. If commentators do not first verify the realities in seeking after the regular garrison and local indigenous troops, and instead abruptly declare that mobilized reinforcements and hired recruits can be dispensed with, it is like a sick man who has not yet stored up aged mugwort (ai) for moxibustion and yet dismisses a physician from afar: should the illness flare up, to then anxiously pack up provisions and go seeking him would be all too late!

Even so, the affairs of the world have their pivotal mechanism (ji); if one grasps that mechanism and sets it in motion, even ten thousand li away there will be none who do not respond. As for the policy of training, Your Excellency (zhishi) is indeed concerned that it may fail to match reality. If the Dynasty regards military affairs as a matter of grave importance, and in times of leisure takes precautions like preparing rags of cloth for caulking leaks [?; yiru, from the Book of Changes, Jiji], we should request…

title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
勑禮官儒臣講究周官及漢唐宋遺制本開元
禮註而增損之爲一代講武之禮每歲冬
月請
駕親閲諸軍而振舉之令行焉則四方聞之孰
敢不鋭志殫力桓桓之貔虎湯湯之江漢
可計日而盛矣況謀臣勇士懐敵愾報國
之心者天下不少若人惟視上之輕重者
何如耳誠重之又何戎政之足慮云武弁
之士計畫踈淺惟執事者其可否焉
===
第二問
祝國泰
馬上中七箭
步下中二箭
制兵有一定之法用兵有無窮之變夫兵
果可以法言乎兵凶器而無法以制之則
散散則棄民兵又果可以法盡乎兵無形
而弗變以通之則泥泥則縱敵此二者廣
將之所守而敵人之所希而求也故兵者
punctuated:
勑禮官、儒臣講究《周官》及漢、唐、宋遺制，本《開元禮》註而增損之，爲一代講武之禮。每歲冬月，請駕親閲諸軍而振舉之令行焉。則四方聞之，孰敢不鋭志殫力？桓桓之貔虎、湯湯之江漢，可計日而盛矣。況謀臣、勇士懐敵愾報國之心者，天下不少。若人惟視上之輕重者何如耳。誠重之，又何戎政之足慮云？武弁之士，計畫踈淺，惟執事者其可否焉。

第二問
祝國泰
馬上中七箭，步下中二箭。

制兵有一定之法，用兵有無窮之變。夫兵果可以法言乎？兵，凶器；而無法以制之則散，散則棄民。兵又果可以法盡乎？兵，無形；而弗變以通之則泥，泥則縱敵。此二者，廣將之所守，而敵人之所希而求也。故兵者，
translation_en:
…issue an imperial command to the ritual officials and Confucian ministers to thoroughly investigate the Rites of Zhou (Zhouguan) and the surviving institutions of the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties, taking the commentary to the Kaiyuan Ritual Code (Kaiyuan li) as a basis and adding to or subtracting from it to establish the martial review ritual for our own dynasty. Every year in the winter months, we should request that His Majesty in person inspect the various armies and put into effect commands to rouse and invigorate them. Then, when the four quarters hear of this, who would dare not sharpen their resolve and exhaust their strength? Martial warriors like fierce tigers and grand armies surging like the Yangzi and Han rivers can be expected to flourish within a matter of days. Moreover, strategic ministers and brave warriors who harbor a spirit of shared hostility toward the enemy and a desire to repay the state are not few in the realm. Such men only look to see how lightly or heavily those above regard them. If they are truly valued, what need would there be to worry over military administration? As a man of the military cap, my plans are crude and shallow; I pray Your Excellency will judge their merits.

Question 2
Zhu Guotai 祝國泰
Mounted archery: 7 hits. Pedestrian archery: 2 hits.

In organizing troops there are fixed methods; in employing troops there are inexhaustible variations. Can warfare really be spoken of in terms of fixed methods? Weapons are instruments of ill omen; yet if there is no method to regulate them, the troops will scatter, and scattering them is to abandon the people. On the other hand, can warfare really be exhausted by fixed methods? Warfare has no constant form; yet if one does not adapt and变通 (vary to suit circumstances), one becomes rigid, and rigidity lets the enemy escape. These two faults are what mediocre [?] generals cling to, and what the enemy hopes and seeks for. Therefore, warfare…

title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
詭道也亦古法也合奇正而一之者是爲
節制之兵而古之所以安民離奇正而二
之者是爲無制之兵而後之所以黷武昔
者聖人作易以象萬物之宜地中有水其
名曰師而制兵之法已寓於此故曰行險
而順順者正也而曰險則有危道焉孔子
於戰則愼之而行三軍則與好謀而成曰
謀則有權存焉險而順謀而成則變而亦
不詭於法矣法以制之變以用之詭設物
===
象紛綸變合雖神智有不能窺而非聖人
亦莫能作世之儒者顧言奇兵有異於仁
義而遂以此爲譎豈知先王制兵以安天
下之意哉在周之興太公實繕其法岐都
井畝之制卽牧野虎賁之師其後齊人得
其遺法管仲修之以相桓公而伯諸侯晉
文襲齊桓之謀以教其民卒繼齊伯孔子
於春秋並叙其績左氏所載可攷也請試
言之齊桓之始伯也嘗九合諸侯矣于貫
punctuated:
詭道也，亦古法也。合奇正而一之者，是爲節制之兵，而古之所以安民；離奇正而二之者，是爲無制之兵，而後之所以黷武。昔者聖人作《易》，以象萬物之宜，地中有水，其名曰「師」，而制兵之法已寓於此。故曰：「行險而順。」順者，正也；而曰「險」，則有危道焉。孔子於戰則愼之，而行三軍則與「好謀而成」。曰「謀」，則有權存焉。險而順，謀而成，則變而亦不詭於法矣。法以制之，變以用之，詭設物象，紛綸變合，雖神智有不能窺，而非聖人亦莫能作。世之儒者，顧言奇兵有異於仁義，而遂以此爲譎，豈知先王制兵以安天下之意哉！
在周之興，太公實繕其法，岐都井畝之制，卽牧野虎賁之師。其後齊人得其遺法，管仲修之以相桓公而伯諸侯；晉文襲齊桓之謀以教其民，卒繼齊伯。孔子於《春秋》並叙其績，左氏所載可攷也。請試言之：齊桓之始伯也，嘗九合諸侯矣。于貫
translation_en:
…is a way of deception, yet it is also the ancient method. Uniting the unorthodox and the orthodox into one makes for a disciplined and regulated army, which was how the ancients brought peace to the people; separating the unorthodox and the orthodox into two makes for an unregulated army, which was how later ages wantonly engaged in warfare. In antiquity, when the sages created the Book of Changes (Yi) to represent the appropriateness of all things, the hexagram showing water within the earth was named "The Army" (Shi), and the method of regulating troops was already embodied therein. Thus it says: "Treading in danger and yet remaining compliant." "Compliant" means orthodox; yet in speaking of "danger," there is a perilous way within it. Confucius was cautious regarding warfare, and when marching with the Three Armies, he favored one "who is fond of strategy and brings it to completion." In speaking of "strategy," tactical adaptability (quan) is preserved therein. Treading in danger while remaining compliant, and employing strategy to bring about completion—thus one adapts to change without violating the method. Regulating troops through method and employing them through adaptation—deceptively setting up physical formations that intricately shift and combine—is something that even godlike intelligence cannot fathom, and that none but a sage could devise. Yet the Confucians of the world say instead that unorthodox military tactics differ from benevolence and righteousness, and consequently regard them as mere trickery. How could they understand the intention of the former kings in regulating troops to bring peace to all under heaven!

During the rise of the Zhou, the Grand Duke (Taigong) truly perfected its methods; the well-field system of the capital at Qi was itself the army of Brave Warriors at Muye. Thereafter, the people of Qi obtained his surviving methods, and Guan Zhong cultivated them to assist Duke Huan and make him hegemon over the feudal lords. Duke Wen of Jin adopted the strategies of Huan of Qi to instruct his people, and ultimately succeeded Qi as hegemon. Confucius recorded the achievements of both in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu), and what is recorded by Mr. Zuo (Zuoshi) can be examined for verification. title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
之盟服江黃也以侵蔡召諸侯志不在蔡
也致勤于鄭振中夏之威會于陽穀停遠
國之信然後按兵于陘退舍召陵而遂於
是請盟矣嘗按兵法攷之合諸侯之師同
次于陘大衆厚集其陣所謂聚而爲正也
江人黃人各守其地彼此相爲犄角所謂
分而爲奇也而夫子謂之正者非以其不
戰屈人之兵有聲罪致討之意乎晉文之
繼伯也又嘗再合諸侯矣始而分曹衛之
===
田以畀宋者激楚之怒也繼而私許復曹
衛者致楚之戰也舟僑先歸則戮之以殉
于國祁滿姦命則殺之以殉諸侯然後楚
殺得臣叔武受盟而楚於是褫氣矣又嘗
按法攷之始退舍以避其師繼伐木以益
其衆莫非其奇之用也然而少長有禮三
軍迭出則正未嘗不在其中而夫子謂之
譎者非以其多方以誤之謀皆純用徂詐
之術乎然齊桓管仲謀之二十餘年一匡
punctuated: 之盟，服江、黃也；以侵蔡召諸侯，志不在蔡也；致勤于鄭，振中夏之威；會于陽穀，停遠國之信。然後按兵于陘，退舍召陵，而遂於是請盟矣。嘗按兵法攷之：合諸侯之師同次于陘，大衆厚集其陣，所謂聚而爲正也；江人、黃人各守其地，彼此相爲犄角，所謂分而爲奇也。而夫子謂之正者，非以其不戰屈人之兵，有聲罪致討之意乎？晉文之繼伯也，又嘗再合諸侯矣：始而分曹、衛之田以畀宋者，激楚之怒也；繼而私許復曹、衛者，致楚之戰也；舟僑先歸，則戮之以殉于國；祁滿姦命，則殺之以殉諸侯。然後楚殺得臣，叔武受盟，而楚於是褫氣矣。又嘗按法攷之：始退舍以避其師，繼伐木以益其衆，莫非其奇之用也；然而少長有禮，三軍迭出，則正未嘗不在其中。而夫子謂之譎者，非以其多方以誤之謀，皆純用徂詐之術乎？然齊桓、管仲謀之二十餘年，一匡
translation_en:
… [the covenant at] Guan was to bring the states of Jiang and Huang into submission; when he summoned the feudal lords to invade Cai, his ambition was not really directed at Cai; he exerted efforts on behalf of Zheng to rouse the prestige of the central states; and he met at Yanggu to secure the good faith of distant states [? 停遠國之信]. Only after this did he halt his troops at Xing and withdraw a stage to Shaoling, whereupon [Chu] consequently requested a covenant. If we examine this according to the principles of the art of war: uniting the armies of the feudal lords to encamp together at Xing and massing a great host to solidify their formations is what is called "concentrating to form the regular (*zheng*) force"; having the men of Jiang and the men of Huang each defend their own territories, acting as mutual supporting horns to one another, is what is called "dividing to form the extraordinary (*qi*) force." Yet the Master [Confucius] called him "upright" (*zheng*)—was it not because he subdued the enemy's troops without fighting, embodying the principle of openly proclaiming their offenses to carry out a punitive expedition?

When Duke Wen of Jin succeeded to the hegemony, he too twice assembled the feudal lords: at first, his dividing the fields of Cao and Wei to give them to Song was to provoke the anger of Chu; subsequently, his privately promising to restore Cao and Wei was to draw Chu into battle. When Zhou Zai [? 舟僑, standardly Zhou Zhiqiao 舟之僑] returned home first, he executed him and paraded his body throughout the state as a warning; when Qi Man [? 祁滿, standardly顛頡 Dian Xie or 祁瞞 Qi Man] violated orders, he killed him and paraded his body before the feudal lords. Only after this did Chu execute Dechen, Shuwu [of Wei] accept the covenant, and Chu thereupon lose heart. If we again examine this according to military methods: first retreating by stages to avoid their army, and then felling trees to augment his forces [by dragging brushwood to raise dust], were nothing other than uses of the extraordinary (*qi*); yet in that the young and the elders observed ritual propriety and the Three Armies advanced in orderly turns, the regular (*zheng*) was never absent from among them. And yet the Master called him "crafty" (*jue*)—was it not because his plans to mislead the enemy in manifold ways all purely employed the arts of trickery and deceit?

Nevertheless, Duke Huan of Qi and Guan Zhong planned for more than twenty years to bring order [to the realm]…

title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
天下而其後叛者九起楚人滅黃已不能
救晉文反國五年而用其民一戰而伯至
其後嗣而楚猶不能與爭其功業不同何
耶說者謂齊桓之楚雖曰猾夏猶未偃然
與中國爭盖夷之始盛也故齊桓得徐爲
之謀晉文之楚則親執中國盟主而在會
諸侯不敢與之抗此夷之極盛也故晉文
不得不急與之戰愚謂召陵之次一得屈
完之盟而退師城濮之役不致敗楚而不
===
已盖桓公所爲特以服楚之心而晉文之
舉則終能摧楚之勢用兵不同而其有功
於中國一也伯德既衰戰伐日行後之言
兵者前莫過於韓信後莫盛於孔明淮陰
遇高祖知人之君登壇一拜首以還定三
秦爲言誠識天下之大勢矣其伐魏也陳
兵臨晉而渡於夏陽遠而示之近也其破
趙也出師井陘而還軍泜上置之死而生
也濰水半濟而擊龍且先聲傳檄而降燕
punctuated:
天下，而其後叛者九起，楚人滅黃，已不能救；晉文反國五年而用其民，一戰而伯，至其後嗣，而楚猶不能與爭，其功業不同，何耶？說者謂齊桓之楚，雖曰猾夏，猶未偃然與中國爭，盖夷之始盛也，故齊桓得徐爲之謀；晉文之楚，則親執中國盟主，而在會諸侯不敢與之抗，此夷之極盛也，故晉文不得不急與之戰。愚謂召陵之次，一得屈完之盟而退師；城濮之役，不致敗楚而不已。盖桓公所爲，特以服楚之心；而晉文之舉，則終能摧楚之勢。用兵不同，而其有功於中國一也。
伯德既衰，戰伐日行。後之言兵者，前莫過於韓信，後莫盛於孔明。淮陰遇高祖知人之君，登壇一拜，首以還定三秦爲言，誠識天下之大勢矣。其伐魏也，陳兵臨晉而渡於夏陽，遠而示之近也；其破趙也，出師井陘而還軍泜上，置之死而生也；濰水半濟而擊龍且，先聲傳檄而降燕、
translation_en:
… the realm, yet afterward nine rebellions arose, and when the men of Chu destroyed Huang, he was already unable to save it. Duke Wen of Jin returned to his state, and after five years he was able to employ his people; with a single battle he became hegemon, and down to his descendants Chu was still unable to contend with them. Why were their achievements so different? Commentators say that the Chu faced by Duke Huan of Qi, though it could be said to disturb the Chinese states, did not yet arrogantly contend with the Central States, for the barbarians were only beginning to grow strong; thus Duke Huan of Qi was able to make his plans at a measured pace. The Chu faced by Duke Wen of Jin, however, personally seized the leader of the covenant of the Central States, and the feudal lords present at the assembly did not dare to resist it; this was the peak of barbarian power, so Duke Wen of Jin had no choice but to fight them urgently. In my humble view, at the encampment at Shaoling, as soon as a covenant was obtained from Qu Wan, the army withdrew; in the campaign of Chengpu, they did not stop until they had inflicted defeat upon Chu. For what Duke Huan did was merely to win the submission of Chu's heart, whereas the action of Duke Wen of Jin was ultimately able to crush Chu's power. Their use of military force differed, yet their merit toward the Central States was one and the same.
Once the virtue of the hegemons declined, warfare and punitive expeditions were carried out daily. Among those in later times who spoke of military affairs, in earlier days none surpassed Han Xin, and in later days none was more illustrious than Kongming [Zhuge Liang]. When the Marquis of Huaiyin [Han Xin] met Gaozu [of Han], a ruler who knew men, upon ascending the altar and receiving his appointment, he spoke first of returning to pacify the Three Qin; truly he understood the great strategic balance of the realm! In his campaign against Wei, he arrayed his troops at Linjin but crossed the river at Xiayang—making what was far off appear near. In his destruction of Zhao, he led his army out through Jingxing and stationed his troops with their backs to the Zhi River—placing them in a fatal position so that they would survive. title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
代皆出奇制變之兵也而信本多多益辦
非其奇以出正乎孔明輔昭烈信義之主
隆中之遇卽陳取荊益之謀亦誠識天下
之大勢矣觀其結好孫權以成與國之援
七擒孟獲以絕內顧之虞祁山一出而拔
三郡散關再戰而馘王雙皆堂堂正正之
陣也而亮本天下奇才非其正以出奇乎
然信佐高祖五載而滅項籍定天下大率
皆信之功而亮雖慮漢賊不兩立終其身
===
不免偏安於蜀都亦功業不同何耶說者
謂信本袴下之流平日名太早而成安君
輩以臭乳之流當之故信得乘其無備不
意而取之孔明負卧龍之望平日名太高
而司馬懿以善筭之雄又畏而自守故孔
明不得以致人而與之戰愚則以爲孔明
本王佐之才而爲興復之舉出師二表忠
義激烈視司馬懿輩眞如婦人渭上之屯
已不復爲退計而營星遽殞是則天也而
punctuated: 代，皆出奇制變之兵也；而信本多多益辦，非其奇以出正乎？孔明輔昭烈信義之主，隆中之遇，卽陳取荊益之謀，亦誠識天下之大勢矣。觀其結好孫權以成與國之援，七擒孟獲以絕內顧之虞，祁山一出而拔三郡，散關再戰而馘王雙，皆堂堂正正之陣也；而亮本天下奇才，非其正以出奇乎？然信佐高祖，五載而滅項籍，定天下大率皆信之功；而亮雖慮漢賊不兩立，終其身不免偏安於蜀都，亦功業不同，何耶？說者謂信本袴下之流，平日名太早，而成安君輩以臭乳之流當之，故信得乘其無備不意而取之；孔明負卧龍之望，平日名太高，而司馬懿以善筭之雄，又畏而自守，故孔明不得以致人而與之戰。愚則以爲孔明本王佐之才，而爲興復之舉，出師二表，忠義激烈，視司馬懿輩眞如婦人。渭上之屯，已不復爲退計，而營星遽殞，是則天也，而
translation_en: … and Dai—all of these were operations that deployed the unorthodox to master changing circumstances. Yet since Han Xin was fundamentally one who could handle all the more troops the more he had, was this not his use of the unorthodox to bring forth the orthodox? Kongming [Zhuge Liang 諸葛亮] assisted Zhaolie [Liu Bei 劉備], a ruler of good faith and righteousness. At their meeting in Longzhong, he immediately set forth the plan to take Jing and Yi provinces, truly recognizing the grand strategic trend of the realm. Observe how he forged an alliance with Sun Quan 孫權 to secure the aid of an allied state, captured Meng Huo 孟獲 seven times to eliminate the worry of internal threats behind him, took three commanderies upon his first expedition from Mount Qi, and took the head of Wang Shuang 王雙 in a second battle at Sanguan—all of these were grand, dignified, and orthodox battle formations. Yet since Liang was fundamentally an extraordinary talent of the realm, was this not his use of the orthodox to bring forth the unorthodox? Nevertheless, when Han Xin assisted Gaozu, within five years he destroyed Xiang Ji 項籍, and the pacification of the realm was largely Han Xin's achievement; whereas although Liang was ever mindful that the Han and the traitors could not both stand, to the end of his life he could not avoid remaining in partial sovereignty in the capital of Shu. That their achievements were also so different—why is this? Some commentators say that Han Xin originalmente came from the ranks of one who had crawled between another's legs, so his reputation in ordinary times was too lowly [reading 早 for 卑?], and men like the Lord of Cheng'an [Chen Yu 陳餘] treated him as a mere wet-behind-the-ears youth; thus Han Xin was able to take advantage of their unpreparedness and catch them by surprise to defeat them. Kongming, on the other hand, bore the renown of the Sleeping Dragon; his reputation in ordinary times was too high, and Sima Yi 司馬懿, as a shrewd and calculating warlord, feared him and held fast to defense, so Kongming was unable to draw the enemy out to engage him in battle. In my humble view, however, Kongming fundamentally possessed the talent of a kingly counselor and undertook the enterprise of restoration. In his two Memorials on Dispatching the Troops (Chushi biao 出師表), his loyalty and righteousness were fierce and stirring, and he truly regarded the likes of Sima Yi as mere women. title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
人何尤蓋信所值者天命所授之君而亮
所遭者炎劉旣燼之運時勢之殊而成敗
非所論也愚嘗統而論之兵以正合以奇
勝大小相錯鈎落相連步數定於地行綴
應于天若管仲寄軍令於內政孔明以八
陣握奇文所謂節制之兵兵之不可敗者
也或利而誘或亂而取或怒而撓或卑而
驕機會成于呼吸虛實反於指顧若韓信
援幟以疑敵先軫曳柴以敗荆所謂變動
之兵兵之必於勝者也善用兵者無不正
亦無不奇奇變而爲正正變而爲奇始於
一分而二變而至於不可勝窮惟明君賢
將爲能用之唐太宗謂先出合戰爲正後
出制勝爲奇而李靖則謂大衆所合爲正
將所自出爲奇以此歎諸將不知奇正之
用蓋靖所傳者本孔明之遺法而六花之
制卽八陣之變也後世知奇正之用者又
孰過於李靖者乎歐陽公五代史敘王彥
punctuated: 人何尤？蓋信所值者，天命所授之君；而亮所遭者，炎劉旣燼之運。時勢之殊，而成敗非所論也。愚嘗統而論之：兵以正合，以奇勝。大小相錯，鈎落相連，步數定於地，行綴應于天，若管仲寄軍令於內政、孔明以八陣握奇文，所謂節制之兵，兵之不可敗者也。或利而誘，或亂而取，或怒而撓，或卑而驕，機會成于呼吸，虛實反於指顧，若韓信援幟以疑敵、先軫曳柴以敗荆，所謂變動之兵，兵之必於勝者也。善用兵者，無不正，亦無不奇；奇變而爲正，正變而爲奇，始於一，分而二，變而至於不可勝窮，惟明君賢將爲能用之。唐太宗謂先出合戰爲正，後出制勝爲奇；而李靖則謂大衆所合爲正，將所自出爲奇，以此歎諸將不知奇正之用。蓋靖所傳者，本孔明之遺法，而六花之制，卽八陣之變也。後世知奇正之用者，又孰過於李靖者乎？歐陽公《五代史》敘王彥
translation_en:
… how can man be blamed? For what Han Xin encountered was a sovereign endowed with the Mandate of Heaven, whereas what Zhuge Liang met with was the fortune of the fiery Liu house already burned to ashes. Their times and circumstances were different, so success and failure are not the basis on which to judge them.

I have tried to synthesize and discuss this as a whole: In warfare, one engages with the orthodox (zheng) and wins through the unorthodox (qi). Large and small units interlock, hooks and links connect to one another, the number of paces is fixed upon the ground, and the alignment of ranks corresponds to Heaven—like Guan Zhong 管仲 embedding military command within civil administration, or Kongming 孔明 mastering the unorthodox pattern through the Eight Formations. These are what are called disciplined troops—troops that cannot be defeated. Sometimes one entices the enemy with gain, sometimes one seizes them when they are in disorder, sometimes one provokes them into agitation, and sometimes one feigns humility to make them arrogant; opportunities are seized in a single breath, and emptiness and substance are reversed in the blink of an eye—like Han Xin 韓信 planting red banners to confuse the enemy, or Xian Zhen 先軫 dragging brushwood to defeat Chu. These are what are called adaptable troops—troops that are certain to win.

For one who is skilled in employing troops, there is nothing that is not orthodox, and nothing that is not unorthodox. The unorthodox transforms into the orthodox, and the orthodox transforms into the unorthodox; beginning from one, it divides into two, and transforms until it is inexhaustible. Only an enlightened sovereign and a worthy general are capable of employing this. Emperor Taizong of Tang 唐太宗 said that going out first to join battle is the orthodox, while coming out afterward to secure victory is the unorthodox; whereas Li Jing 李靖 said that where the main host joins battle is the orthodox, and what the general devises on his own is the unorthodox, sighing on this account that the various generals did not understand the use of the unorthodox and the orthodox. Indeed, what Li Jing transmitted was originally the legacy method of Kongming, and his Six-Petal formation was none other than a variation of the Eight Formations. Among those in later ages who understood the use of the unorthodox and the orthodox, who could surpass Li Jing?

title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
章德勝之戰期以三日破敵聞者皆竊笑
及破南城果三日是時莊宗在魏聞彥章
復用料其必速攻自魏疾馳來救已不及
矣莊宗之善料彥章之出奇何其神也公
以此歎當時諸將不能用奇蓋有感於西
夏之事而云然而在今日亦有然者愚竊
謂制兵有法而用兵有術法者常用以待
敵者也術者出奇以勝敵者也備之於無
事之時寧可無奇不可無正不幸而值有
===
事之時爲正不及不可無奇蓋數不能常
實而不虛士不能常勇而無怯糧不能常
足而困匱古之良將或因糧於敵或借勢
於人或驅市人而使之戰雖一陣之間一
軍之將莫不以此而取勝愚嘗居山見山

… [Wang Yan]zhang's (王彥章) battle at Desheng (德勝), he set a deadline of three days to defeat the enemy, and all who heard it secretly laughed. When he broke the Southern Fort, it indeed took three days. At that time, Emperor Zhuangzong (莊宗) was in Wei (魏); hearing that Yanzhang had been reappointed, he calculated that Yanzhang would certainly attack swiftly, and raced from Wei to the rescue, yet was already too late. Zhuangzong's skill in calculation and Yanzhang's deployment of surprise tactics—how miraculous they were! Master Ouyang [Xiu] (歐陽公) used this to lament that the generals of his own time could not employ surprise tactics, speaking out of emotion stirred by the affairs with Western Xia (西夏). Yet at the present day, the same is also true.

I humbly maintain that in organizing troops there are regular rules, and in employing troops there is tactical art. Rules are what one constantly uses to await the enemy; tactical art is what deploys surprise to defeat the enemy. When preparing in times of peace, one would rather lack surprise tactics than lack orthodoxy; when by misfortune one encounters times of crisis and orthodox measures cannot catch up, one cannot be without surprise tactics. For numbers cannot always be solid without weak points, soldiers cannot always be brave without cowardice, and provisions cannot always be sufficient when facing exhaustion and scarcity [?]. The good generals of antiquity sometimes seized provisions from the enemy, sometimes borrowed strategic advantage from others, and sometimes drove marketplace civilians to make them fight. Even within a single battle formation or for the commander of a single army, none failed to win victory by these means.

title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
手曰無虎畏人猶人畏虎吾機設掩所不
備是以獲也因而有悟植木形也鳴金聲
也深菁之所設者實也兵亦類是歟吁徒
實而形與聲不施焉山居備猛獸者之所
不爲而况國乎是故仁義衰而後有節制
節制失而後用奇奇在果果在速此天下
偉男子之所爲非常筭之士所可到也
執事欲聞御兵之要乎在先立吾全勝之
法以示不可犯之威然後用吾制變之術
===
以酬不可測之知如是而已至論其所以
料敵之方制勝之具則愚鄙人也而猶未
能言之也惟
執事進而教之
論
五者知勝之道
杜應雷
馬上中六箭
步下中五箭
punctuated:
手？曰：「無。虎畏人猶人畏虎，吾機設掩所不備，是以獲也。」因而有悟：植木，形也；鳴金，聲也；深菁之所設者，實也。兵亦類是歟！吁！徒實而形與聲不施焉，山居備猛獸者之所不爲，而况國乎？是故仁義衰而後有節制，節制失而後用奇。奇在果，果在速，此天下偉男子之所爲，非常筭之士所可到也。執事欲聞御兵之要乎？在先立吾全勝之法，以示不可犯之威；然後用吾制變之術，以酬不可測之知，如是而已。至論其所以料敵之方、制勝之具，則愚鄙人也，而猶未能言之也，惟執事進而教之。

論

五者知勝之道

杜應雷
馬上中六箭，步下中五箭。
translation_en:
… technique?” He replied, “No. A tiger fears a man just as a man fears a tiger; I set my traps to catch them where they are unprepared, and therefore I capture them.” From this I came to a realization: planting wooden stakes is outward form (xing); sounding gongs is声 (sound/reputation, sheng); and what is set up in the deep thickets is substance (shi). Is warfare not just like this? Alas! Relying solely on substance without employing form and reputation is something even mountain dwellers guarding against fierce beasts would not do—how much less a state! Therefore, when benevolence and righteousness decline, there is disciplined regulation; when disciplined regulation fails, one uses the unorthodox (qi). The unorthodox lies in decisiveness, and decisiveness lies in speed. This is the deed of a great hero in the world, not something a man of ordinary calculations can attain. Does Your Excellency wish to hear the essentials of commanding troops? It lies in first establishing our method for complete victory so as to display an inviolable majesty, and only then employing our art of controlling changing circumstances so as to fulfill unfathomable wisdom—nothing more than this. As for discussing the specific methods for estimating the enemy and the instruments for securing victory, I am a rustic person and am not yet able to speak of them; I only pray that Your Excellency will bring me forward and instruct me.

Discourse

“These five are the way to know victory” (Wu zhe zhi sheng zhi dao)

title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
古之善用兵者全之而已矣而非破之也善用
其全者形之而已矣而非戰之也夫兵者勝而
後戰非戰而後勝也勝而後戰者未戰而形已
具我形之敵必從之則可措因形之勝矣是知
勝者也戰而後勝者未知勝負之所在而逞於
一决之間其不勝者破軍殺將傷天地之和其
勝者殺士糜民違仁義之心是不知勝者也非
先王制兵之本意矣善用兵者觀敵之形而定
其謀攻人之國而不事戰故未戰而勝已具旣
===
戰而勝以全知此者可與言將矣吁吾讀孫武
子書見其兵押闔變化者不可究詰而要其所
以勝者五而名之曰謀攻之篇其旨在全軍爲
上破軍次之意其猶有先王之遺意宜其爲兵
家稱首而後世莫能廢之歟蓋嘗論之兵之爲
道其動有機機者以形設以計用機之所在在
敵則敵勝在我則我勝是故地無大小兵無强
弱有小國弱兵而見畏於天下者機在焉故也
吾觀敵之形不示吾所形故能因形以制勝吾
punctuated: 古之善用兵者，全之而已矣，而非破之也；善用其全者，形之而已矣，而非戰之也。夫兵者，勝而後戰，非戰而後勝也。勝而後戰者，未戰而形已具，我形之，敵必從之，則可措因形之勝矣，是知勝者也。戰而後勝者，未知勝負之所在，而逞於一决之間。其不勝者，破軍殺將，傷天地之和；其勝者，殺士糜民，違仁義之心。是不知勝者也，非先王制兵之本意矣。善用兵者，觀敵之形而定其謀，攻人之國而不事戰，故未戰而勝已具，旣戰而勝以全。知此者，可與言將矣。吁！吾讀孫武子書，見其兵押闔變化者不可究詰，而要其所以勝者五，而名之曰《謀攻》之篇，其旨在全軍爲上，破軍次之。意其猶有先王之遺意，宜其爲兵家稱首，而後世莫能廢之歟！蓋嘗論之，兵之爲道，其動有機。機者，以形設，以計用。機之所在，在敵則敵勝，在我則我勝。是故地無大小，兵無强弱，有小國弱兵而見畏於天下者，機在焉故也。吾觀敵之形，不示吾所形，故能因形以制勝；吾
translation_en:
Those of antiquity who were skilled in using the military simply kept things intact rather than shattering them; those skilled in achieving wholeness simply shaped the tactical disposition rather than engaging in battle. For in warfare, one first secures victory and only then goes to battle; one does not first go to battle and then seek victory. When one secures victory before going to battle, the tactical disposition is already complete before fighting begins; when we shape the disposition, the enemy is compelled to follow it, and thus victory derived from that disposition is assured—this is what it means to know victory. Those who go to battle and only then seek victory do not yet know where victory or defeat lies, yet stake everything on a single decisive clash. If they do not win, their armies are shattered and their generals slain, injuring the harmony of Heaven and Earth; even if they win, soldiers are slaughtered and the people are ground down, violating the mind of benevolence and righteousness. Such men do not know victory, and this was not the original intent of the Former Kings in instituting military forces. Those skilled in using the military observe the enemy's disposition to determine their strategy, attacking another's state without resorting to pitched battle; therefore, before fighting begins, victory is already assured, and once battle is joined, victory is achieved with everything intact. One who understands this is worthy of discussing generalship!

Alas! When I read the book of Master Sun Wu (Sunzi), I see that the opening and closing [?] and transformations of his military art are unfathomable, yet he summarizes the ways to victory in five points and titles the chapter "Planning Offensives" (Mougong). Its central purport is that preserving an army intact is best, while shattering an army is second-best. One suspects that it still preserves the lingering intent of the Former Kings—how fitting that he is acclaimed as the foremost of the military strategists, and that later generations have been unable to discard his work!

I have previously discussed this: as a Way, the movement of the military hinges upon a pivotal mechanism (ji). This pivotal mechanism is established through tactical disposition and employed through calculation. Wherever the pivotal mechanism resides—if it is with the enemy, the enemy wins; if it is with us, we win. Therefore, regardless of whether territory is large or small, or whether troops are strong or weak, the reason a small state with weak troops can be feared throughout the realm is that the pivotal mechanism resides with it.
