title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
觀敵之用不出吾所用故能致用以成功其爲
道生於天地而行乎陰陽者也今夫天地之大
德曰生生以春夏而成以秋冬其出以機其入
以機所謂雷霆霜雪者非天之威武以震曜乎
天下者耶而天猶不亟亟然用之藏出於入畜
陽於陰此天地之所以用其機者人之於兵也
亦然故知機之用者勝矣知勝之道者全矣夫
兵不能廢攻攻不能無戰然攻者不止於攻其
城伐其陣而已必有攻其心之要焉戰者非徒
列其陣齊其衆而已必守吾氣而有待焉攻其
心者所謂知彼者也守吾氣而有待者所謂知
己者也形之於無窮而要之則有五而已故曰
色不過五五色之變不可勝視也聲不過五五
聲之變不可勝聽也味不過五五味之變不可
勝嗜也勝不過五五勝之變不可勝用也是故
知敵之可與戰而戰之者先人有奪人之心也
知不可與戰而不戰者後人有待其衰者也長
勺之戰曹劌所以先登而成牢之役知瑩所以
punctuated: 觀敵之用，不出吾所用，故能致用以成功。其爲道，生於天地而行乎陰陽者也。今夫天地之大德曰生，生以春夏而成以秋冬，其出以機，其入以機。所謂雷霆霜雪者，非天之威武以震曜乎天下者耶？而天猶不亟亟然用之，藏出於入，畜陽於陰，此天地之所以用其機者；人之於兵也亦然。故知機之用者勝矣，知勝之道者全矣。夫兵不能廢攻，攻不能無戰。然攻者，不止於攻其城、伐其陣而已，必有攻其心之要焉；戰者，非徒列其陣、齊其衆而已，必守吾氣而有待焉。攻其心者，所謂知彼者也；守吾氣而有待者，所謂知己者也。形之於無窮，而要之則有五而已。故曰：色不過五，五色之變，不可勝視也；聲不過五，五聲之變，不可勝聽也；味不過五，五味之變，不可勝嗜也；勝不過五，五勝之變，不可勝用也。是故知敵之可與戰而戰之者，先人有奪人之心也；知不可與戰而不戰者，後人有待其衰者也。長勺之戰，曹劌所以先登；而成牢之役，知瑩所以
translation_en: …observe the enemy's operations without revealing my own operations, and therefore I can bring operations to bear and achieve success. As a Way, it originates in Heaven and Earth and operates through yin and yang. Now, the great virtue of Heaven and Earth is called life-giving: it gives life in spring and summer and brings completion in autumn and winter; its emergence is through the pivotal mechanism, and its withdrawal is through the pivotal mechanism. Are not what we call thunderbolts, frost, and snow the martial majesty by which Heaven awes and dazzles all under Heaven? Yet Heaven still does not employ them hastily, concealing emergence within withdrawal and storing yang within yin. This is how Heaven and Earth employ their pivotal mechanism, and so it is too with human beings in warfare. Therefore, one who knows the use of the pivotal mechanism will be victorious, and one who knows the Way of victory will keep his forces whole. Now, in warfare one cannot dispense with attack, and in attack one cannot avoid battle. Yet attacking does not stop merely at assaulting their walls and striking their formations; there must be the essential point of attacking their minds. Doing battle is not merely a matter of drawing up one's formations and aligning one's multitude; one must guard one's own spirit and await the right moment. Attacking their minds is what is called knowing the other; guarding one's own spirit and awaiting the right moment is what is called knowing oneself. These manifest in inexhaustible ways, yet in essence there are only five. Therefore it is said: the colors do not exceed five, yet the permutations of the five colors are more than can ever be seen; the tones do not exceed five, yet the permutations of the five tones are more than can ever be heard; the flavors do not exceed five, yet the permutations of the five flavors are more than can ever be tasted; the factors of victory do not exceed five, yet the permutations of the five factors of victory are more than can ever be used up. For this reason, to know that the enemy can be fought and to fight him is to forestall others with a mind that seizes their spirit; to know that he cannot be fought and not to fight is to move after others while waiting for their decline. In the Battle of Changshao, this was how Cao Gui 曹劌 advanced to the fore; and in the Campaign of Chenglao [?], this was how Zhi Ying 知瑩…

title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
避楚也衆而用之者分之而莫知所從也寡而
用之者疑之而爭其所之也孫臏減竈以示弱
虞詡增竈以示强是也師克在和而韓信之入
秦也從東歸之士田單之破齊也因將士之怒
師貴在虞而趙奢一夜而奪閼與李愬夜半而
入蔡州凡此皆將之能而君又不得而御焉若
穰苴斬莊賈以立威而吳起戮寵隊以示嚴乃
楚魏之君不怒而國以强故君貴於任將將貴
乎知勝也將而知勝非深而靜神而明者不足
===
以語於此故曰知幾其神乎夫彼數國者非兵
弱也非戰不善也敝在於不知其勝之所在而
卒爲人致故力屈勢窮而身不免爲虜而曹劌
知瑩趙奢田單韓信之數子者得以全其勝而
收其功夫攻之所以欲用其謀者夫固欲其全
之而非欲其破之也是故我欲戰敵雖怯而其
勢不得不與我戰我不欲戰敵雖强其勢不得
與我戰戰不戰之形爭於敵而機存乎我也藏
其爭使人不爭完其戰使人不戰又吾之所以
punctuated: 避楚也。衆而用之者，分之而莫知所從也；寡而用之者，疑之而爭其所之也。孫臏減竈以示弱，虞詡增竈以示强是也。師克在和，而韓信之入秦也，從東歸之士；田單之破齊也，因將士之怒。師貴在虞，而趙奢一夜而奪閼與，李愬夜半而入蔡州。凡此皆將之能，而君又不得而御焉。若穰苴斬莊賈以立威，而吳起戮寵隊以示嚴，乃楚、魏之君不怒而國以强。故君貴於任將，將貴乎知勝也。將而知勝，非深而靜、神而明者，不足以語於此。故曰：「知幾其神乎！」夫彼數國者，非兵弱也，非戰不善也，敝在於不知其勝之所在，而卒爲人致，故力屈勢窮而身不免爲虜；而曹劌、知瑩、趙奢、田單、韓信之數子者，得以全其勝而收其功。夫攻之所以欲用其謀者，夫固欲其全之，而非欲其破之也。是故我欲戰，敵雖怯，而其勢不得不與我戰；我不欲戰，敵雖强，其勢不得與我戰。戰不戰之形爭於敵，而機存乎我也。藏其爭使人不爭，完其戰使人不戰，又吾之所以
translation_en: … avoided Chu. To employ forces when numerous is to divide them so that the enemy does not know where to follow; to employ forces when few is to sow doubt among the enemy so that they contend over where one is going. Sun Bin 孫臏 reducing his camp stoves to feign weakness, and Yu Xu 虞詡 increasing his camp stoves to feign strength, are examples of this. An army's triumph lies in harmony: thus when Han Xin 韓信 entered Qin, he followed soldiers who longed to return east; when Tian Dan 田單 broke the enemy in Qi, he relied on the fury of his officers and men. An army prizes preparedness and surprise: thus Zhao She 趙奢 seized Yanyu 閼與 in a single night, and Li Su 李愬 entered Caizhou 蔡州 at midnight. All of these belong to the capability of the general, and the ruler must not interfere by trying to control him from afar. Consider how Rangju 穰苴 executed Zhuang Jia 莊賈 to establish his authority, and Wu Qi 吳起 executed a favored officer of the ranks to demonstrate strictness [?], yet the rulers of Chu and Wei were not angered, and their states thereby grew strong. Therefore, in a ruler what is prized is trusting his general, and in a general what is prized is knowing how to achieve victory. For a general to know how to achieve victory, unless he is profound and calm, unfathomable and perspicacious, he is unworthy to speak of this. Hence it is said: "To know the subtleincipience of things—surely that is divine!" Now, as for those several defeated states, it was not that their troops were weak, nor that they were unskilled in battle; their flaw lay in not knowing where victory resided, so that in the end they were manipulated by others. Thus, their strength exhausted and their position desperate, they themselves could not escape becoming captives; whereas those several men—Cao Gui 曹劌, Zhi Ying 知瑩, Zhao She, Tian Dan, and Han Xin—were able to keep their victories intact and reap their achievements. Now, the reason one wishes to use strategy in attacking is assuredly because one desires to preserve the target intact rather than shatter it. Therefore, when I wish to give battle, even if the enemy is cowardly, his situation compels him to fight me; when I do not wish to give battle, even if the enemy is strong, his situation prevents him from fighting me. The outward form of fighting or not fighting is contested with the enemy, yet the decisive mechanism rests with me. To conceal one's contention so that others do not contend, and to keep one's battle-readiness complete so that others do not fight—this, moreover, is the means by which I …

title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
謀爲攻而不以攻爲攻者也吾觀戰國用兵者
流大率不知民之司命而反殘民以逞白起詐
坑於長平項籍暴戮於函谷殺機一發天地反
覆不惟仁義之用不行而節制之兵亦罔聞若
武者亦戰國知謀之士而其爲法獨有志於全
軍安國之道其一篇之中三致意焉較之好戰
以逞者其利害有間矣而孟氏猶曰我善爲陳
我善爲戰大罪也蓋以仁義視節制則桓文固
湯武之罪人以節制視知謀則武又在管仲之
===

誠不可廢也夫吁亦衰世之意夫
又

馬上中七箭

則其機常握於我而可以決勝於未戰之先矣
punctuated:
謀爲攻，而不以攻爲攻者也。吾觀戰國用兵者流，大率不知民之司命，而反殘民以逞。白起詐坑於長平，項籍暴戮於函谷，殺機一發，天地反覆。不惟仁義之用不行，而節制之兵亦罔聞。若武者，亦戰國知謀之士，而其爲法，獨有志於全軍安國之道，其一篇之中三致意焉。較之好戰以逞者，其利害有間矣。而孟氏猶曰：「我善爲陳，我善爲戰，大罪也。」蓋以仁義視節制，則桓、文固湯、武之罪人；以節制視知謀，則武又在管仲之下也。雖然，古法不可復矣。世之驅不敎之民以戰，而糜軍殃民者，其流弊至今烈焉，則武之法誠不可廢也夫！吁，亦衰世之意夫！
又
張國華
馬上中七箭
步下中五箭
制勝之策，恒預圖之難者也。善師者得其要焉，則其機常握於我，而可以決勝於未戰之先矣。
translation_en:
… strategy as the means of attack, rather than using direct assault as the attack. When I observe the likes of those who employed the military during the Warring States period, for the most part they did not understand what governs the lives of the people, and instead mutilated the people to gratify their own ambitions. Bai Qi 白起 treacherously buried troops alive at Changping 長平; Xiang Ji 項籍 brutally slaughtered soldiers at Hangu 函谷. Once the impulse to kill was unleashed, heaven and earth were overturned. Not only was the application of benevolence and righteousness not practiced, but even disciplined and regulated troops were unheard of. Someone like Sun Wu 孫武 was also a man of resourceful strategy in the Warring States era, yet in establishing his methods, he alone set his mind on the way of preserving the army whole and securing the state, repeatedly emphasizing this point three times within a single chapter. Compared to those who delighted in warfare to gratify themselves, there is a clear difference between its benefits and harms. Yet Mencius (Mengshi 孟氏) still said: "Those who say 'I am adept at drawing up battle formations, I am adept at waging war' are great criminals." Indeed, when disciplined warfare is viewed from the standpoint of benevolence and righteousness, Duke Huan 桓 and Duke Wen 文 are assuredly criminals in the eyes of Tang 湯 and Wu 武; and when resourceful strategy is viewed from the standpoint of disciplined warfare, Sun Wu in turn ranks below Guan Zhong 管仲. Even so, the ancient methods cannot be restored. In the world, those who drive uninstructed people into battle, thereby ruining armies and bringing calamity upon the people, have perpetuated abuses that remain fierce to this day; thus Sun Wu's methods truly cannot be discarded! Alas, this too is a sentiment belonging to an age of decline!

A strategy for securing victory is something that is always difficult to plan in advance. When one who is skilled in leading troops grasps its essentials, the decisive mechanism is constantly held in our own hands, and victory can be determined before battle is even joined.…

title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
何則兵家之事紛然其至繁而兵家之用淵然
其至變爲將者以一人而司之欲使勝筭常在
我而不失而且制之於事機之未形此豈非天
下之甚難者乎以天下之所共難而吾獨能以
擅其長則必有道焉矣乃善於用兵者惟執其
要而悉於圖焉操之易簡而非泥籌之詳審而
匪疎審攻守之宜明多寡之節恊將卒之志而
且有備無患進退無所制焉夫如是則其謀裕
其氣振天下莫之或先而吾可以無敵於天下
===
斯所謂決勝於未戰而制勝於已然者乎五者
知勝之道孫子於謀攻之篇終言之也夫攻也
而必先於謀謀也而必圖其勝五者誠不可或
已而亦誠不容有加者乎是故爲將帥以臨敵
孰不欲戰之全勝也亦孰不欲勝之預知也然
利鈍之異時險易之殊勢衆寡堅脆之不齊其
力決必勝之謀於兩陳之間其爲難也乂矣況
夫縱横闔闢萬變靡常奇正虛實羣情罔測盖
有非吾一人之智力所能制者吾聞勝負無常
punctuated:
何則？兵家之事，紛然其至繁；而兵家之用，淵然其至變。爲將者以一人而司之，欲使勝筭常在我而不失，而且制之於事機之未形，此豈非天下之甚難者乎？以天下之所共難，而吾獨能以擅其長，則必有道焉矣。乃善於用兵者，惟執其要而悉於圖焉：操之易簡而非泥，籌之詳審而匪疎；審攻守之宜，明多寡之節，恊將卒之志，而且有備無患，進退無所制焉。夫如是，則其謀裕、其氣振，天下莫之或先，而吾可以無敵於天下。斯所謂決勝於未戰，而制勝於已然者乎！

「五者，知勝之道」，孫子於《謀攻》之篇終言之也。夫攻也而必先於謀，謀也而必圖其勝，五者誠不可或已，而亦誠不容有加者乎！是故爲將帥以臨敵，孰不欲戰之全勝也？亦孰不欲勝之預知也？然利鈍之異時，險易之殊勢，衆寡、堅脆之不齊其力，決必勝之謀於兩陳之間，其爲難也乂矣。況夫縱横闔闢，萬變靡常，奇正虛實，羣情罔測，盖有非吾一人之智力所能制者。吾聞「勝負無常」
translation_en:
Why is this so? The affairs of military strategists are multitudinous and supremely complex, while the applications of military strategy are profound and supremely changeable. For a commander to oversee them as a single individual, wishing to ensure that the winning calculation always remains in our hands without fail, and moreover to control it before the crucial opportunity has even taken form—is this not something extremely difficult in the world? When something is universally difficult for the world, yet we alone are able to excel at it, there must be a way to it. Thus, those skilled in the use of troops simply grasp what is essential and are thorough in their planning: handling it with ease and simplicity rather than rigidity, and calculating it with careful deliberation rather than carelessness; examining the appropriateness of offense and defense, clarifying the measure of large and small forces, harmonizing the resolve of generals and soldiers, and moreover being prepared so as to avoid calamity, with advance and retreat unconstrained by anyone. When it is like this, one's plans are ample and one's morale is roused; none in the world can anticipate us, and we can be unmatched in the world. Is this not what is meant by determining victory before the battle is fought, and securing victory when it has already come to pass!

"These five are the way to know victory"—Sunzi spoke of this at the conclusion of the chapter "Planning Offensives" (Mougong). Now, in attacking one must put planning first, and in planning one must aim for victory; these five things truly cannot be dispensed with, nor can anything be added to them! Therefore, among those who act as commanders facing the enemy, who does not desire complete victory in battle? And who does not desire foreknowledge of victory? Yet sharpness and bluntness vary with the times, rugged and easy terrain differ in situational advantage, and superior or inferior numbers, strong or fragile forces are unequal in their strength; to determine a plan for certain victory between two arrayed armies has long [乂=久?] been difficult. How much more so when maneuvers in length and breadth, opening and closing, undergo myriad changes without constancy, and the unorthodox and orthodox, the empty and solid, are beyond the fathom of ordinary minds—for there are things that cannot be controlled by the intelligence and strength of a single person like oneself. I have heard the saying that "victory and defeat have no constancy"…

title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
之說矣吾聞常勝之家難與料敵之說矣此而
曰五者爲知勝之道其言若龜卜燭照而不可
易毋乃孫子之侈於談乎非也若孫子者亦據
夫要機以示多筭之長策而已矣今夫息喧爭
之口者必諭之以利害之要辭剖煩劇之治者
必齊之以畫一之要政決勝負於彼已而勝常
在我者必持之以不況不踈之要策彼遇敵以
戰爲常者也然可戰則當急擊而勿失不可戰
則當全師以待釁此非料敵之要乎吾而得之
===
則攻守之勝筭在我者可知也用兵以多爲貴
者也然或易地則當用衆隘地則當用寡或衆
則疊出以疲敵或寡則選鋒以先登此非審形
之要乎吾而得之則調發之勝謨在我者可知
也紛然三軍恒欲其畏我而不畏敵也然視如
嬰兒可以赴深溪視如赤子可以與俱死此非
附衆之要乎吾而得之則聯屬之勝計在我者
可知也至若睹患于未形防難於未著懷暮夜
有戎之患嚴濡有衣袽之戒則以虞待不虞自
punctuated: 之說矣，吾聞常勝之家難與料敵之說矣。此而曰五者爲知勝之道，其言若龜卜燭照而不可易，毋乃孫子之侈於談乎？非也，若孫子者，亦據夫要機以示多筭之長策而已矣。今夫息喧爭之口者，必諭之以利害之要辭；剖煩劇之治者，必齊之以畫一之要政；決勝負於彼已而勝常在我者，必持之以不況不踈之要策。彼遇敵以戰爲常者也，然可戰則當急擊而勿失，不可戰則當全師以待釁，此非料敵之要乎？吾而得之，則攻守之勝筭在我者可知也。用兵以多爲貴者也，然或易地則當用衆，隘地則當用寡；或衆則疊出以疲敵，或寡則選鋒以先登，此非審形之要乎？吾而得之，則調發之勝謨在我者可知也。紛然三軍，恒欲其畏我而不畏敵也，然視如嬰兒可以赴深溪，視如赤子可以與俱死，此非附衆之要乎？吾而得之，則聯屬之勝計在我者可知也。至若睹患于未形，防難於未著，懷暮夜有戎之患，嚴濡有衣袽之戒，則以虞待不虞，自
translation_en: … the saying [that victory and defeat have no constant], and I have heard the saying that a family that is constantly victorious is difficult to assess the enemy with. When here he says that these five things are the way to know victory, speaking as though by tortoise-shell divination or candlelight illumination that cannot be altered—is this not Sunzi boasting in his discourse? Not so. One like Sunzi simply relies on the essential pivot-points to demonstrate the superior strategy of many calculations, and nothing more. Now then, one who quiets clamorous and contentious mouths must instruct them with essential words regarding advantage and harm; one who cuts through complex and burdensome governance must unify it with essential policies of uniform administration; and one who decides victory and defeat between the enemy and oneself so that victory always rests with us must uphold essential strategies that are neither extravagant [?] nor lax. When encountering an enemy, engaging in battle is the norm; yet when one can fight, one should strike urgently and not miss the opportunity, and when one cannot fight, one should preserve the army intact and wait for an opening. Is this not the essential point of assessing the enemy? If we grasp this, then it can be known that the victorious calculation of offense and defense rests with us. In employing troops, great numbers are valued; yet in open terrain one should use a multitude, and in narrow terrain one should use a few; or when numerous, send them out in waves to exhaust the enemy, and when few, select vanguard troops to scale the walls first. Is this not the essential point of examining terrain and disposition? If we grasp this, then it can be known that the victorious plan of deployment rests with us. As for the multitudinous Three Armies, one constantly desires that they fear us and do not fear the enemy; yet when one regards them as infants, they can follow one into deep ravines, and when one regards them as beloved children, they can die together with one. Is this not the essential point of winning the allegiance of the multitude? If we grasp this, then it can be known that the victorious stratagem of binding the ranks together rests with us. As for perceiving disaster before it takes form and guarding against peril before it becomes manifest, harboring anxiety over armed attack in the dark of night, and strictly observing the warning of having rags ready for a leak—then in waiting in preparedness for the unprepared, the essential point of self-…

title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
防之要在是矣而以不可勝待敵之可勝者又
非其所預必者乎秉鉞而專征制命於閫外無
掣肘之慮擅獨斷之能則將能而君不御者奪
敵之要在是矣而君臣同心未戰而廟筭勝者
又非其所先得者乎此皆臨戎之長畫應敵之
深機也勝在我則可戰所謂善攻而出于九天
之上者是已勝在彼則可守所謂善守而藏於
九地之下者是已或可戰而亦不恃勝以自逞
則攻矣而未始不善藏其用焉或可守而亦不
===
終怯以自靡則守矣而未始不疾發其機焉微
乎微乎此全勝之道我可得而知敵不可得而
測焉者乎嘗稽之古人之用矣韓信破竹以下
三秦亞夫堅守以疲吳楚此知可與戰而不可
與戰者也而與炎殄逆之勝成矣王翦伐楚以
六十萬謝玄敵秦以八千此識衆寡之用者也
而帝秦疆晉之勝立矣楚王廣狹續之憲吳起
能甘苦之同此均上下之欲者也而定覇强國
之勝擅矣程不識日鳴刁斗李光弼御軍嚴肅
punctuated: 防之要在是矣。而以不可勝待敵之可勝者，又非其所預必者乎？秉鉞而專征，制命於閫外，無掣肘之慮，擅獨斷之能，則將能而君不御者，奪敵之要在是矣。而君臣同心，未戰而廟筭勝者，又非其所先得者乎？此皆臨戎之長畫，應敵之深機也。勝在我則可戰，所謂善攻而出于九天之上者是已；勝在彼則可守，所謂善守而藏於九地之下者是已。或可戰而亦不恃勝以自逞，則攻矣，而未始不善藏其用焉；或可守而亦不終怯以自靡，則守矣，而未始不疾發其機焉。微乎微乎！此全勝之道，我可得而知，敵不可得而測焉者乎！嘗稽之古人之用矣：韓信破竹以下三秦，亞夫堅守以疲吳、楚，此知可與戰而不可與戰者也，而與炎殄逆之勝成矣。王翦伐楚以六十萬，謝玄敵秦以八千，此識衆寡之用者也，而帝秦疆晉之勝立矣。楚王廣狹續之憲，吳起能甘苦之同，此均上下之欲者也，而定覇强國之勝擅矣。程不識日鳴刁斗，李光弼御軍嚴肅，
translation_en:
… the essential point of self-defense lies right here. And waiting for the enemy's vulnerability while making oneself invincible—is this not also what one can be assured of in advance? Holding the battle-axe with sole authority over a campaign, exercising command beyond the threshold of the court without the worry of having one's elbow pulled back, and possessing the capacity for independent decision-making—having a capable general with whom the ruler does not interfere is where the essential point of overcoming the enemy lies. And when ruler and minister are of one mind, achieving victory through the calculations in the ancestral temple before battle is even joined—is this not also what is secured beforehand? All these are far-sighted plans for facing battle and profound stratagems for responding to the enemy. When victory rests with us, we may fight: this is what is meant by "he who is skilled in attack moves as from above the ninefold heavens." When victory rests with them, we may defend: this is what is meant by "he who is skilled in defense hides as under the ninefold earth." Sometimes one is able to fight yet does not presume upon victory to indulge in recklessness; thus, even in attacking, one never fails to skillfully conceal one's capabilities. Sometimes one should defend yet does not remain timid to the end and waste away; thus, even in defending, one never fails to swiftly unleash the decisive mechanism. Subtle, how subtle! Is this not the Way of complete victory, which we can know, but which the enemy can never fathom?

Let us examine how the ancients applied these principles. Han Xin 韓信 split bamboo [in his unstoppable advance] to subjugate the Three Qin 三秦, while Zhou Yafu 周亞夫 held fast to his defenses to exhaust Wu 吳 and Chu 楚: these men knew when to fight and when not to fight, and thus the victories that raised the Han [reading 興炎 for 與炎] [?] and exterminated the rebels were achieved. Wang Jian 王翦 attacked Chu 楚 with six hundred thousand men, while Xie Xuan 謝玄 withstood Qin 秦 with eight thousand: these men understood the employment of large and small forces, and thus the victories that made Qin an empire and strengthened Jin 晉 [reading 彊晉 for 疆晉] were established. The King of Chu 楚王 extended the grace [reading 惠 for 憲] of bestowing floss-padded garments [reading 挾纊 for 狹續] [?], while Wu Qi 吳起 was able to share both sweet and bitter with his troops: these men united the desires of superiors and inferiors, and thus they monopolized the victories that established hegemony and strengthened their states. Cheng Bushi 程不識 sounded the sentry bells by day [and night], and Li Guangbi 李光弼 governed his army with strictness and solemnity: …

title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
此契夫以虞待不虞之法者也而威匈奴復雨
河之勝致矣孫武斬宮嬪而無畏穰苴誅貴臣
而不慴此符於將能而君不御之理者也由是
入郢都振弱齊以取勝于天下又豈不赫然可
稱也哉是故經之以五事本斯立矣而非此無
以善其用校之以七計謀斯長矣而非此無以
成其能蓋知之於未戰之先而勝機以萌知之
於將戰之際而勝筭以定知之于臨戰之時則
百戰不殆者在我矣劑勝負而權彼已樹偉伐
而著威聲善師之道孰能外是而他有所事哉
旨哉孫子識其要而詳言之且審言之也雖然
以此料敵修此五者故全也然四者繫於我而
可以自盡惟將能而不御者繫之君而難以自
持孫子于五者之末舉而終之其意深矣然則
如之何可哉亦曰有鷹揚之太公則必有授鉞
之武有壯猷之方叔則必有寵任之宣爲將者
其亦自殫忠誠以感動人主而已矣是爲論
punctuated: 此契夫「以虞待不虞」之法者也，而威匈奴、復雨河之勝致矣。孫武斬宮嬪而無畏，穰苴誅貴臣而不慴，此符於「將能而君不御」之理者也，由是入郢都、振弱齊，以取勝于天下，又豈不赫然可稱也哉！是故經之以五事，本斯立矣，而非此無以善其用；校之以七計，謀斯長矣，而非此無以成其能。蓋知之於未戰之先，而勝機以萌；知之於將戰之際，而勝筭以定；知之于臨戰之時，則「百戰不殆」者在我矣。劑勝負而權彼已，樹偉伐而著威聲，善師之道，孰能外是而他有所事哉？旨哉！孫子識其要而詳言之，且審言之也。雖然，以此料敵，修此五者故全也。然四者繫於我而可以自盡，惟「將能而不御」者繫之君而難以自持，孫子于五者之末舉而終之，其意深矣。然則如之何可哉？亦曰：有鷹揚之太公，則必有授鉞之武；有壯猷之方叔，則必有寵任之宣。爲將者，其亦自殫忠誠以感動人主而已矣。是爲論。
translation_en: …this tallied with the method of "awaiting the unprepared with preparation," and thus the victories of overawing the Xiongnu and recovering the Two River regions [Lianghe 兩河, transcribed 雨河] were achieved. Sun Wu 孫武 executed the palace concubines without fear, and Sima Rangju 司馬穰苴 put the noble minister to death without trepidation; this conformed to the principle of "having capable generals with whom the ruler does not interfere." Thereby they entered the Chu capital of Ying and revitalized weak Qi to win victory across the realm—how could this not be illustriously worthy of praise! Therefore, when governed by the Five Factors (wushi 五事), the foundation is established, yet without these five conditions of victory there is no way to perfect their application; when appraised by the Seven Considerations (qiji 七計), the strategy excels, yet without these five conditions there is no way to bring their capabilities to fruition. For by knowing them before a war has begun, the opportunity for victory sprouts; by knowing them when about to go to war, the calculation for victory is settled; and by knowing them at the moment of engaging in battle, fighting a hundred battles without peril rests within our grasp. In balancing victory and defeat and weighing the enemy and oneself [reading 已 as 己], in establishing great martial achievements and manifesting an awesome reputation, who in the Way of commanding armies well could depart from these and occupy themselves with anything else? Profound indeed! Master Sun (Sunzi 孫子) recognized what is essential and spoke of it in detail, and spoke of it with care. Even so, in gauging the enemy by these means, it is by cultivating all five of these that perfection is attained. Yet four of them depend upon oneself and can be fulfilled through one's own efforts, whereas "the general being capable and the ruler not interfering" alone depends upon the sovereign and is difficult to control by oneself. That Master Sun raised this at the very end of the five to conclude them shows that his meaning was deep indeed. If that is so, what then should be done? One can only say: if there is a Grand Duke (Taigong 太公) soaring like a hawk, there will surely be a King Wu 武王 who bestows the battle-axe; if there is a Fang Shu 方叔 of grand plans, there will surely be a King Xuan 宣王 who favors and trusts him. Those who serve as generals should simply exhaust their own loyalty and sincerity in order to move the ruler's heart, and nothing more. Such is my discourse.

title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
浙江武舉鄉試錄後序
萬曆癸酉冬十月期當貢武
士于
京師
侍御蕭公如
制舉行式徵諸執事具官以從
度靡不恪所舉士五十人例
===
當有錄伯輪以職事與觀厥
成得序諸末序曰我
國家設武科以網羅天下虎臣
法具今嚴較然與文科埒重
曩歲雖間一報罷旋卽舉行
如故且不限額而
申諭加詳亦以久安長治之策
punctuated:
浙江武舉鄉試錄後序
萬曆癸酉冬十月，期當貢武士于京師，侍御蕭公如制舉行，式徵諸執事，具官以從，度靡不恪。所舉士五十人，例當有錄。伯輪以職事與觀厥成，得序諸末。序曰：我國家設武科以網羅天下虎臣，法具今嚴，較然與文科埒重。曩歲雖間一報罷，旋卽舉行如故，且不限額，而申諭加詳，亦以久安長治之策，
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Zhejiang Military Provincial Examination

In the tenth month, in winter, of the guiyou year of the Wanli era (1573), the time arrived to present military candidates as tribute to the Capital. Investigation Censor Lord Xiao (蕭公) conducted the examination in accordance with the imperial regulations. He formally summoned the various functionaries, who attended in their official capacities, and in every measure none failed to be reverent and diligent. Fifty candidates were selected, and by precedent there should be a published record. Because of my official duties, I, [Zhang] Bolun (伯輪), participated in and witnessed the completion of this affair, and so was permitted to write a postface at the end of the record.

The postface states: Our Dynasty established the military examination system in order to gather in the tiger-like stalwart ministers of the realm. The regulations are complete and the current rules strict [or: the regulations are complete and commands strict], clearly matching the civil service examinations in importance. Although in bygone years the examinations were occasionally suspended, they were soon held again as before; moreover, no fixed quota was imposed, and the repeated imperial instructions were made ever more detailed. This was truly because the strategy for enduring peace and lasting order…

title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
非文武竝用不可也故士之
應格而進升於大司馬者日
益增增衆則四方緩急宜有
可恃决策出奇人人可當大
将軍事矣迺今目所覩記南
北要區列障開府之臣率多
起自行伍而武科之選反遠
謝之即有一二能枕負弋鋋
===
爲
天子揚威萬里外然亦落落如晨
星可數也究其故豈當時騎
步之試非其長技而譚說孫
吴者竟虛語耶嘗讀史至田
單下狄之事深有味乎魯仲
punctuated: 非文武竝用不可也。故士之應格而進升於大司馬者，日益增。增衆則四方緩急宜有可恃，决策出奇，人人可當大将軍事矣。迺今目所覩記，南北要區，列障開府之臣，率多起自行伍，而武科之選反遠謝之。即有一二能枕負弋鋋，爲天子揚威萬里外，然亦落落如晨星可數也。究其故，豈當時騎步之試非其長技，而譚說孫、吴者竟虛語耶？嘗讀史至田單下狄之事，深有味乎魯仲
translation_en: … cannot do without employing both civil and military officials together. Therefore, the candidates who meet the standards and are advanced to the Minister of War (da sima 大司馬) grow more numerous by the day. As their numbers increase, there ought to be men to rely upon in emergencies throughout the four quarters—formulating strategies and devising surprise tactics, each capable of assuming the duties of a Grand General. Yet among what we observe and remember today, the officials who guard the frontier barriers and establish regional commands in key zones of the north and south have mostly risen from the military ranks, whereas those selected through the military examinations fall far behind them. Even if there are one or two who can sleep on their arms and carry arrows and spears, projecting the Son of Heaven's majesty ten thousand li abroad, they can be counted as sparsely as morning stars. Investigating the reason for this, could it be that the tests in mounted and dismounted archery at the time were not their strong suit, and that their discussions of Sun Wu 孫武 and Wu Qi 吳起 were after all mere empty talk? When I once read in the histories of the affair of Tian Dan 田單 conquering Di 狄, I deeply savored Lu Zhong…

title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
連之言何其明於料事而卒
中其勝負之情若此二心不
可以事君疑志不可以應敵
此其理固可預計者也今武
科士未必盡如單而反情異
嚮有生之樂無死之心又比
比而是則其不能敵愾於天
===
下稱封疆之託者又奚足異
云是故邊陲山海不足慮而
所慮者在將將非技藝譚說
之難而忠勇無二之爲難唐
之令公宋之武穆古今名將
材也一則以身爲天下安危
者二十年一說者謂仗忠信安
punctuated: 連之言，何其明於料事，而卒中其勝負之情若此！「二心不可以事君，疑志不可以應敵」，此其理固可預計者也。今武科士未必盡如單，而反情異嚮、有生之樂、無死之心，又比比而是，則其不能敵愾於天下、稱封疆之託者，又奚足異云！是故邊陲山海不足慮，而所慮者在將；將非技藝譚說之難，而忠勇無二之爲難。唐之令公、宋之武穆，古今名將材也。一則以身爲天下安危者二十年，一說者謂仗忠信、安───
translation_en: …[Lu Zhong]lian’s words—how clear-sighted he was in foreseeing events, and how accurately he hit upon the true circumstances of victory and defeat like this! "With a divided heart one cannot serve one's ruler; with a wavering will one cannot face the enemy"—this principle can indeed be anticipated beforehand. Today, candidates in the military examination are not necessarily all the equal of [Tian] Dan, and yet those with shifting sentiments and divergent aims, who take pleasure in living and have no resolve to die, are everywhere to be found. What wonder is it, then, that they are unable to vent righteous indignation against the empire's enemies or live up to the trust of defending the frontiers! Therefore, the frontier mountains and seas are not what give cause for worry; what gives cause for worry is the generals. And with generals, the difficulty lies not in martial skills or theoretical discourse, but in being loyal, brave, and single-hearted. The Lord President of the Secretariat [Guo Ziyi 郭子儀] of the Tang and the Martial and Reverent Prince [Yue Fei 岳飛] of the Song were men of renowned generalship past and present. The one bore upon his own person the safety and peril of the empire for twenty years, and commentators say that because he relied on loyalty and trustworthiness and rested peacefully in…

title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
義命則功業自有所本一則
志抗金人志圖興復而其自
信亦曰盡忠報國焉耳茲諸
士是舉也余兩觀之射繼閱
其所爲文信非武胄之英則
伍閭之儁矣但不二之心人
不可知使他日出而能以委
===
身奉國自許一遇壁壘輙肯
奮距先登則摲曍有需所謂
求矢一心者在是也其所樹
立固未必可與令公武穆比
擬亦豈令行伍輩得先之而
顧處其後乎不然按武舉遺
事蘇明允嘗以爲病此豈
punctuated: 義命，則功業自有所本；一則志抗金人，志圖興復，而其自信亦曰「盡忠報國」焉耳。茲諸士是舉也，余兩觀之射，繼閱其所爲文，信非武胄之英，則伍閭之儁矣。但不二之心，人不可知。使他日出而能以委身奉國自許，一遇壁壘，輙肯奮距先登，則摲曍有需，所謂「求矢一心」者在是也。其所樹立，固未必可與令公、武穆比擬，亦豈令行伍輩得先之而顧處其後乎？不然，按武舉遺事，蘇明允嘗以爲病，此豈
translation_en: …righteousness and destiny,” so his achievements naturally had a foundation; the other set his will on resisting the Jurchens and restoring the dynasty, and the conviction he held for himself was simply “exhausting loyalty to repay the state.” Now, in the selection of these gentlemen, I twice observed them in archery and subsequently reviewed the essays they composed; truly, if they are not the finest of military lineages, then they are the outstanding talents of the local communities and ranks. Yet an undivided heart cannot be known by others. If in the future they go forth into service and can pledge themselves to devote their lives to serving the state—so that the moment they encounter enemy ramparts, they are readily willing to leap forward and be the first to scale them—then there will be that upon which we rely to sweep away the haze [?], and what is called “seeking those who swear to be of one mind” lies right here. Even if what they establish may not necessarily be comparable to the Duke of Ling [Guo Ziyi 郭子儀] or Prince Wumu [Yue Fei 岳飛], how could they let mere rank-and-file soldiers surpass them while they instead lag behind? Otherwise, if one examines the past affairs of the military examinations, Su Mingyun [Su Xun 蘇洵] once regarded them as flawed; how could this be…

title: 萬曆元年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
朝廷懸格購材之意者與夫勇
夫以圖報爲盛節智士以兼
時爲令圖今
龍飛薦士之初天下智勇咸嶽嶽
思奮也諸士平時自抱智勇
今日又遇
侍御公登而進之則竭忠靖
===
獻自託於
日月之光余固知諸士決不忍自
二其心也已詩曰赳赳武夫
公侯干城又曰赳赳武夫公
侯腹心願以是爲諸士誦
浙江等處提刑按察司副使
滕伯輪謹序
punctuated:
朝廷懸格購材之意者與？夫勇夫以圖報爲盛節，智士以兼時爲令圖。今龍飛薦士之初，天下智勇咸嶽嶽思奮也。諸士平時自抱智勇，今日又遇侍御公登而進之，則竭忠靖獻，自託於日月之光，余固知諸士決不忍自二其心也已。《詩》曰：「赳赳武夫，公侯干城。」又曰：「赳赳武夫，公侯腹心。」願以是爲諸士誦。
浙江等處提刑按察司副使滕伯輪謹序。
translation_en:
…the intention of the Imperial Court in establishing standards to seek out talent? Now, the brave man regards planning to repay his country as a grand integrity, while the wise scholar takes seizing the moment [?] as a fine design. Today, at the outset of the Emperor's ascension to the throne and the recommendation of scholars, the wise and brave throughout the realm all stand tall and eager to exert themselves. You scholars ordinarily cherish wisdom and bravery within yourselves, and today you have met with His Excellency the Investigating Censor, who has selected and advanced you; thus, in exhausting your loyalty and calmly offering your service, entrusting yourselves to the radiance of the sun and moon, I certainly know that you scholars could never bear to harbor a divided heart. The Book of Odes (Shijing) says: "Gallant are the warriors, shields and walls for the duke and marquis." And again it says: "Gallant are the warriors, trusted intimates of the duke and marquis." I wish to recite these verses for you scholars.

Respectfully prefaced by Teng Bolun 滕伯輪, Surveillance Vice Commissioner of Zhejiang and Other Places.
